News.title: RAF Typhoons scrambled to UK-bound Qatar Airways flight 'causing concern'
News.content:
RAF Typhoons scrambled to UK-bound Qatar Airways flight 'causing concern'

Flight QR23 from Doha to Manchester Airport caused 'concern to civil authorities' once it reached UK airspace, triggering a 'RAD Quick Reaction Alert'

View Image The RAF launched Typhoons (Image: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Two RAF jets were sent to escort a Qatar Airways flight bound for Manchester from Doha tonight.

‌



The incident occurred as flight QR23 from the Qatari capital Doha to Manchester Airport entered UK airspace. The RAF said in a statement that the aircraft was "causing concern to civil authorities", which triggered the "RAF Quick Reaction Alert".

‌



An RAF spokesperson said: "We can confirm that an RAF Quick Reaction Alert was launched for a Qatar Airways flight which was causing concern to civil authorities. The incident was resolved and the airliner landed safely at Manchester Airport."

Article continues below

Qatar Airways has been approached for comment.

News.title: Essex explosion live: Inferno after huge blast as 100 firefighters tackle flames
News.content:
More than 100 firefighters are tackling a massive fire at a farm off Southend Road between East Hanningfield and Rettendon in Essex

A massive explosion at a farm in Essex has shaken buildings up to 15 miles away, with footage showing an enormous ball of flames erupting from the scene.

Essex County Fire and Rescue Service said more than 100 firefighters are at the scene of a "large industrial unit fire" off Southend Road between East Hanningfield and Rettendon, near Chelmsford.

The blaze, which is understood to be at Highlands Farm, has been declared a major incident because of its size. East of England Ambulance Service said it is responding to a "significant incident", and police have cordoned off a huge area around the blaze.

"If you live or are travelling nearby, please continue to keep your windows and doors closed," the fire service said. "Please avoid the area while we deal with this incident."

Did you see or hear the explosion? If so, please get in touch by emailing livenews@reachplc.com

News.title: Andy Burnham rules out calling snap General Election and will plough on with Labour's manifesto
News.content:
Andy Burnham rules out calling snap General Election and will plough on with Labour's manifesto

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ruled out a snap General Election, and said the government "needed to focus on making the country work" instead, claiming going to the polls would "postpone" that work

View 4 Images Andy Burnham during a meeting at No 10 North, in Manchester, on Friday (Image: Christopher Furlong/Pool Getty v)

Andy Burnham has shut down the idea of calling a snap election just days after he was sworn in as Prime Minister.

‌



Mr Burnham said he would push forward with Labour's election winning 2024 manifesto, while opening a new headquarters for the centre of Government in Manchester, dubbed the Number 10 North. The former Mayor of Manchester has become the seventh British Prime Minister in 10 years but has said no to another General Election anytime soon.

‌



When asked if he was considering calling a snap election for the country, Mr Burnham said: "No I'm not. I don't think that is right."

‌



Andy Burnham says rates cut is his way of backing venues he loved as youngster READ MORE :

View 4 Images Andy Burnham inside No 10 North on the opening day (Image: Christopher Furlong/PA Wire)

The new Prime Minister said the government's focus is currently on "making the country work".

The PM told the Manchester Evening News: "We live in a parliamentary democracy. There was a manifesto in 2024. I'm sticking to that manifesto. I'm bringing forward my version but it is still within that manifesto. I just think that we need to focus on making the country work.

‌



"That is the biggest priority right now. A general election would postpone that essential work. I'm also trying to do politics differently, as I did when I was mayor of Greater Manchester."

View 4 Images Andy Burnham and wife Marie-France van Heel pose for photos outside 10 Downing Street, on July 20 (Image: Dinendra Haria/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

Before becoming PM, Burnham was asked if he would call an early election, while taking part in an Ask Me Anything (AMA) on Reddit. On July 3, the Makerfield MP also ruled this out and wrote: "No. As I said in my speech on Monday, I’m going to work to the 2024 manifesto."

‌



On Friday, Mr Burnham opened the No 10 North at Heron House in the centre of Manchester, where he is expected to work once a week during his premiership.

The Labour Party leader said his move to have a base in the north was about "rebalancing power in the country".

Mr Burnham was joined at the opening by Chancellor John Healey, First Secretary of State Louise Haigh, and the country’s top civil servant, Cabinet Secretary Antonia Romeo.

‌



View 4 Images Mr Burnham during a National Economic Council at No 10 North (Image: Christopher Furlong/Pool Getty v)

He later held a meeting with local leaders, including English regional mayors like Liverpool's Steve Rotheram and Greater Lincolnshire's Andrea Jenkyns. Mr Burnham argued the new northern headquarters would help save money.

The Prime Minister said: "Is it a gimmick? Well, the fact that I was there today with the Chancellor, the cabinet secretary, the First Secretary of State, the Transport Secretary - a large part of the government was there in Manchester with me today.

Article continues below

"And the fact of us being there, taking decisions there, just means that we're rebalancing power in the country aren't we? And the benefits that will fall to Manchester are massive. But it's about No 10 North taking power out of Whitehall and putting it into all parts of the country. That’s its job."

On Friday, Mr Burnham also revealed a separate, similar forum would be arranged with the leaders of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, which he described as a "different form of devolution".

Mr Burnham also revealed his feelings towards his new role saying: "I love the job". The Prime Minister said: "You can't ever prepare for it because you can't ever know what it's like until you do it, but... I'm getting used to it very quickly because you have to. So I'm in at the deep end, but I've started swimming and I've enjoyed it so far."

News.title: Met Office puts 12 areas on alert for 'heavy bursts' of rain on Sunday
News.content:
Met Office puts 12 areas on alert for 'heavy bursts' of rain on Sunday

Heavy bursts of rain are set to hit parts of the UK through Saturday night into Sunday morning, a Met Office meteorologist has said

View 3 Images Heavy rain is set to hit parts of the UK (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

The Met Office says multiple parts of the UK should brace for heavy rain on Monday ahead of what is forecast to be a fourth heatwave of the year next week.

‌



A total of 12 UK areas have been told to expect heavy downpours by 5am on Sunday. Meteorologist Alex Burkill said: "The weather front will bring some more widespread rain through Saturday night into Sunday, especially towards the northwest, where it could be a bit heavy, a bit persistent and down the western side [of England], some heavier bursts of rain.

‌



"Some parts of Wales and South West England are likely to see more rain through Saturday night into Sunday than they have done so far this month."

‌



View 3 Images A Met Office map showing which areas will be covered by rainfall on Sunday morning (Image: Met Office)

On Sunday, there will be "outbreaks of showery rain" in many places at 10am , with "a lot of the rain" then clearing away towards the east, Mr Burkill said. There will still be some "fair scattering of showers" across Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern parts of England and Wales around 3pm but this will be "a bit less rain than earlier on in the day", he added.

Mr Burkill said: "More sunshine across southern areas looking largely fine by the time we get into the afternoon [on Sunday]. Temperatures are going to be down a few degrees compared to what we've seen of late.

‌



"Most places will be a couple of degrees lower than on Saturday. Temperatures will peak in the mid-twenties. High pressure in the south means more dry weather next week and we could see a return of the heat."

News.title: Westminster Bridge live: Four police officers seriously injured in Thames boat crash
News.content:
A police boat carrying armed cops has crashed near Westminster Bridge in central London, leaving five officers injured - four seriously - after a number plunged into the River Thames.

Emergency services have swarmed the scene in central London, with responders from the RNLI seen treating casualties on a boat at the pier.

A large number of police officers, fire crews and ambulances are also at the scene, and traffic across the bridge came to a standstill with the Underground also impacted.

Metropolitan Police Commander Nick John said: "Our thoughts are with all those involved, in particular our officers who were injured and those who responded in challenging circumstances.

"The four officers who remain in hospital have serious but non-life-threatening injuries. We will give them all every support as they recover."

News.title: Cairngorms wildfire declared major incident as hundreds flee their homes
News.content:
Cairngorms wildfire declared major incident as hundreds flee their homes

Police Scotland has declared a major incident as fire crews continue to battle a massive wildfire within the Cairngorms National Park that is nearing the village of Nethy Bridge

View 3 Images Police Scotland have declared the wildfire in the Cairngorms National Park a major incident (Image: Highland, Islands, Moray and Aberdeenshire Weather/Facebook)

Police Scotland has declared a major incident as firefighters battle a huge wildfire within the Cairngorms National Park, with hundreds evacuated from homes in its path.

‌



The force said strengthening winds have made the fire more unpredictable and caused it to spread towards Nethy Bridge, a small village in the Strathspey area of the park, prompting the decision to declare a major incident.

‌



All residents of Nethy Bridge are being evacuated as a precaution and directed to a respite centre at the Macdonald Aviemore Resort. Access roads into the village have been closed.

‌



The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) has deployed more than 500 firefighters since the wildfire was first reported on July 15. Crews have been supported by specialist wildfire appliances, all-terrain vehicles, helicopter water-bombing operations and partner agencies.

View 3 Images The wildfire in the Cairngorms National Park pictured on July 21 (Image: Rachel Keenan/PA Wire)

Essex explosion live: Inferno after huge blast as 100 firefighters tackle flames READ MORE :

Westminster Bridge live: Multiple casualties in horror police boat crash on Thames READ MORE :

Superintendent Judy Hill, from Police Scotland, said: "The weather conditions experienced within the Cairngorms over the last 24 hours have added further complexities to this situation. With evidence suggesting the fire is spreading towards Nethy Bridge, the decision has been taken to declare a major incident and evacuate residents as a precaution."

‌



She said additional police officers are being deployed to help people leave their homes and maintain cordons around restricted areas.

"We understand this is a very concerning time for residents, businesses and visitors to the Cairngorms region," Supt Hill said. "Please be assured that the multi-agency response remains fully committed to bringing this incident to a safe conclusion as quickly as possible."

Deputy Assistant Chief Officer Kenny Barbour, from the SFRS, said firefighters, specialist resources and partners have "worked tirelessly" over the past nine days to respond to this "challenging and complex wildfire".

‌



View 3 Images More than 500 firefighters have been mobilised since the wildfire was first reported

He said: "The combination of prolonged dry conditions, strengthening winds and challenging terrain has created an extremely complex operational environment. Large areas of the fire ground are inaccessible by vehicle or on foot, making helicopter water-bombing operations and specialist wildfire tactics essential to our response."

Mr Barbour also thanked Forestry and Land Scotland, the Cairngorms National Park Authority, landowners, estate gamekeepers and emergency service partners for their expertise and local knowledge, which he said had been "invaluable" in protecting communities and the natural environment.

Article continues below

He urged people to continue following the advice of Police Scotland and to stay away from the affected areas while firefighters tackle the wildfire.

News.title: PlayStation Network goes down worldwide as thousands unable to connect servers
News.content:
Video game giant Sony has confirmed that all PlayStation services were 'experiencing issues' amid thousands of reports from users around the globe

Gamers around the world, including thousands in the UK, reported issues with the PlayStation Network, with many saying they were unable to connect to the server.

Problems started around 11.30am today (Friday, July 24) with video game giant Sony later confirming all PlayStation services were "experiencing issues". It added that it was working to resolve the problem as soon as possible and thanked users for their patience. The firm has not yet given a reason for the outage.

Tens of thousands of network problem reports had been logged in the UK on outage-tracking website Downdetector.

One frustrated UK user wrote on Downdetector: "Can't load any digital games at all bought or free. Can't connect to servers to verify licences, doesn't matter what I try to load - I get the same message every time."

News.title: Law student is charged over intercepted bomb in car
News.content:
A 25-year-old law student has appeared in court charged over a bomb which was discovered in a car in the Republic of Ireland.

Isobella Perrie Sullivan, from Abbeylands Park in Clane, County Kildare, was charged with the possession of explosives.

It was alleged she was driving the car which was intercepted by gardaÃ­ (Irish police) near Carrickmacross, County Monaghan, on Wednesday.

A defence solicitor told the court his client had been asked to take a bag to Northern Ireland and had not been aware what was in it.

Earlier on Friday, gardaÃ­ (Irish police) told reporters their interception was part of an operation targeting dissident republican activity.

The accused, who was arrested on Wednesday, was brought before a special sitting of Trim District Court in County Meath on Friday evening.

A member of the Garda Special Detective Unit told the court the car she was driving was stopped by officers on N2 at Aclint, south of Carrickmacross.

News.title: Huge explosion and fire rip through Essex industrial site
News.content:
A huge explosion triggered by a fire spreading to a store of fertiliser tore through an industrial unit in Essex on Friday, with more than 100 firefighters sent to tackle a massive fire and a "major incident" declared.

Footage which captured the moment of the explosion showed a ball of flames erupting into the air and people fleeing, while witnesses told BBC News the sound was "like a bomb" and as loud as a "sonic boom".

A number of buildings and vehicles on farmland were gutted by the fire, which was expected to keep burning into Saturday.

People living near the fire - which happened close to the village of Rettendon, south of Chelmsford - were urged to keep their windows closed as smoke spread.

News.title: Man describes trying to save mother and daughter who drowned off Essex beach
News.content:
A day-tripper has told the BBC how he dived into the sea in an attempt to save a mother and daughter who drowned off an Essex beach.

Craig Bowe, 42, battled the incoming tide at West Mersea, near Colchester, three times after hearing screams on Wednesday evening.

The kitchen fitter, who was on a day trip from Hertfordshire to celebrate his daughter's 10th birthday, managed to haul Shally and Samiha Rahman from the waves and also helped a seven-year-old boy onto a lifeboat.

Despite his efforts, the pair - aged 41 and 15 - died in the desperate attempt to bring the boy to shore.

The boy, who became stranded during a family day out from Barking, east London, was airlifted to hospital and remained there in a critical condition on Friday.

Three others were taken by ambulance to another hospital after the incident unfolded at about 17:35 BST.

News.title: Heatwave reveals lost archaeological sites across Wales
News.content:
Lost archaeological sites have emerged in grasslands across Wales after a prolonged spell of hot and dry weather.

Wales has seen about 5% of the average rainfall for July, after a series of back-to-back heatwaves and a drier than usual April to June. A drought has also been triggered in parts of Wales.

Experts said these dry conditions have brought to light a range of hidden archaeological remains, including Roman buildings and practice trenches from World War One.

Many are only visible from the air as distinctive marks in crops and grass, with some not being seen for "two or three decades", according to the Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments of Wales (RCAHMW).

News.title: Officers hurt as police boat hits Westminster Bridge
News.content:
Five Metropolitan Police officers have been injured after a police boat struck Westminster Bridge in central London.

The Met said the incident occurred at about 15:40 BST and involved a boat from the Marine Policing Unit which was carrying armed officers.

One officer has since been discharged from hospital and the others have serious but non-life-threatening injuries.

The police confirmed that no members of the public were involved or injured in the crash.

The police boat was responding to a report of a person in the water near Battersea.

The Met said in a statement: "As a result of the collision, three officers were thrown from the boat into the water. They were recovered by those on nearby boats.

"Additional officers responded alongside the London Ambulance Service and London Fire Brigade."

The Met's Cmdr Nick John thanked river users "who came to the aid of the officers, as well as other police and emergency service colleagues who immediately made their way to the scene to assist".

He added: "The quick-thinking and professionalism of all those involved undoubtedly prevented any further injuries."

News.title: Angela Rayner rules out rent controls in England
News.content:
Housing Secretary Angela Rayner has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is not looking at bringing in rent controls in England.

She told BBC Breakfast that changes made through the Renters' Rights Act, which came into effect in May, were "already having a significant impact on the market".

She added that controls which had been implemented in some areas of the UK over the past few years had not "necessarily brought rents down".

In 2023 when he was the mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham called for freezes to private sector rents until the cost of living crisis was over.

But Rayner told the BBC on Friday: "I don't think that rent freezes, rent controls, is a way forward at the moment.

"Three years ago, Andy called for that because there was a significant crisis in the rental market.

"We implemented between then the Renters' Rights Act which is giving renters more power and control."

Temporary rent controls were introduced in Scotland in October 2022 but expired last year.

Under new legislation, ministers in Holyrood will be able to designate certain places in Scotland as rent control areas - expected to come in by 2027.

Councils will be able to cap rent increases on some properties at a maximum of 6%.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski has said he wants to see rent controls brought in for all rented property in England.

Responding to Rayner's interview, he described Burnham as "continuity Starmer", posting on X: "The new prime minister talks a lot of about helping with the cost of living crisis. This is the one single measure that would help the most and save billions. All talk."

Jeremy Corbyn, who pledged to bring in rent controls during the 2019 general election when he was the Labour leader, described Rayner's announcement as "extremely disappointing".

"There is no hope of ending homelessness if we do not stand up to vested interests and take action against extortionate private rents.

"We need rent controls, and we need them now."

Sir Sadiq Khan, the mayor of London, has also long called on the government to implement a cap.

But Gareth Bacon, the Conservative's shadow housing minister, said rent controls would be "disastrous" and "intensify the damage done by Labour's agenda that has driven landlords from the market and reduced choice for renters".

"Labour are clearly divided. Burnham's pick for housing secretary has disowned a policy he himself has repeatedly backed," he said.

The term rent controls describes a range of measures a government can implement - from capping price increases to freezing them for a period of time.

Landlord groups say they may exacerbate the housing crisis by putting owners off renting out property.

The Renters' Rights Act was brought in to give more stability and security to the 11 million people who rent from private landlords.

Under the legislation, fixed-term tenancies have been banned and it is now significantly harder for landlords to evict tenants.

Rents can also only be increased once a year to the property's "open market rent".

News.title: NBA superstar LeBron James to join Philadelphia 76ers
News.content:
LeBron James has announced he will be joining the Philadelphia 76ers next season for what he says will be his final contract in the NBA.

The 41-year-old, the highest points scorer in the history of the league, left the Los Angeles Lakers after eight years last month.

The Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves and Miami Heat were also rumoured to be in the running for the four-time NBA champion.

"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energise a new fanbase and start this incredible journey one last time," James said on X., external

James has won an NBA title with all three teams he previously played for. He won two with Miami, who earlier this week mistakenly posted a link to an 'introductory press conference' for James.

A Heat spokesperson told Reuters, external the video was posted in error by staff who were preparing for the possibility of James rejoining the team he played for between 2010 and 2014.

Either side of that Miami stint, James had two spells with Cleveland, who drafted James in 2003 and are based near his hometown of Akron, Ohio.

"Miami I'll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always [be] home," James added.

James helped the Cavs become NBA champions in 2016 and joined the Lakers in 2018, claiming another NBA title two years later.

He has been named the NBA's Most Valuable Player four times, all between 2009 and 2013, and has been an NBA All-Star the last 22 seasons running.

News.title: Police declare 'major incident' as wind change increases Cairngorms wildfire risk
News.content:
Police Scotland has declared a major incident as emergency services continue to tackle a wildfire which has been burning in the Cairngorms National Park for 10 days.

The force said it followed "a significant change in weather conditions" which has increased the risk of fire spreading towards the village of Nethy Bridge.

All Nethy Bridge residents have been evacuated to allow emergency services to continue their response.

Smoke from the wildfire can now be seen 59 miles away in Aberdeen following a change in wind direction.

Supt Judy Hill said: "The weather conditions experienced within the Cairngorms over the last 24 hours have added further complexities to this situation.

"With evidence suggesting the fire is spreading towards Nethy Bridge, the decision has been taken to declare a major incident and evacuate residents as a precaution.

"Additional police resources are being deployed to assist in contacting those who need to leave their properties and to maintain cordons around restricted areas while our fire service colleagues continue to tackle the wildfire."

News.title: Slapping therapist jailed over death 'released early'
News.content:
An alternative healer jailed over the death of a woman at one of his workshops has been released from prison just 18 months into a 10-year sentence, it is understood.

Hongchi Xiao, 63, from California, was convicted and sentenced in 2024 for the manslaughter by gross negligence of 71-year-old Danielle Carr-Gomm in 2016.

Carr-Gomm, who was diabetic, died while taking part in a therapy event in Wiltshire, which involved people being slapped or slapping themselves repeatedly.

On Friday, during a Court of Appeal hearing where an application to overturn his conviction was quashed, it emerged Xiao had been returned to the US and was believed to no longer be in custody.

In his judgment, Lord Justice Dingemans said it seemed Xiao had been returned to the US on 2 July through the Early Removal Scheme.

This enables eligible foreign national offenders to be deported from the UK once they have served the minimum required proportion of their sentence.

However, he added: "Other information suggests he was deported on 30 June 2026. It seems that Mr Xiao is not in custody in the USA."

A government spokesperson said: "Hongchi Xiao's crimes were terrible, and our thoughts remain with his victims.

"This government is deporting foreign national offenders at pace, with more than 5,000 deported last year, and Hongchi Xiao is prohibited from ever returning to the UK."

They added if Xiao were to return to the UK, he will be liable to serve the rest of his sentence from the point he was deported.

News.title: Southport killer Axel Rudakubana appears to be manipulating the system, families' lawyer says
News.content:
A lawyer for the families of the children murdered by Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has said his transfer from prison to a psychiatric hospital may be an attempt to "manipulate the system".

Rudakubana, 19, was given a life sentence for the murder of three children - Alice da Silva Aguiar, 9, Bebe King, 6, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, 7 - and attempted murder of eight other children and two adults.

On Thursday, he was moved from HMP Belmarsh to Broadmoor psychiatric hospital in Berkshire.

Prisoners who are considered to present a risk to staff, inmates or themselves because of mental disorders can be moved to hospital under the Mental Health Act.

Next Wednesday marks two years since Rudakubana carried out the attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class on 29 July 2024.

Lawyer Chris Walker, who represents the three bereaved families, said they "don't believe the merits" of the transfer on the basis of a mental health issue and is calling for more information from ministers.

"In my mind this is a new event, this is something which occurred whilst he was at prison, and we at this stage don't believe the merits of it in terms of him because I've seen no evidence at all until today which suggests he has a significant mental health disorder," Walker told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

He added: "We do have an evil person but being evil does not mean that you're suffering with psychosis of some sort.

"We need to know is this a single event, is this a recurring event, is this him playing the system and we need those answers."

The Prison Officers' Association told the BBC that Rudakubana was transferred due to a deterioration in his mental health.

Walker added in a separate statement that the news would "devastate" the families at any time but "the fact that this has occurred as we approach the second anniversary in our view is another move by AR who would appear to be attempting, once again, to manipulate the system".

He continued: "We have been given the barest of details and whilst we are supporting the families through this we are urgently seeking a meeting with the appropriate authorities to understand the situation before commenting further."

A lawyer for the families of the attack's survivors said they did not want to give "notoriety" to Rudakubana and that attention should be focused on supporting the children around the anniversary.

Nicola Ryan-Donnelly of Fletchers Solicitors said: "The focus of public outrage should not be on moves that this perpetrator has made, it should be examining how we are two years on from this attack and some of these girls are still not receiving the proper psychological care and support that they should be to recover from this."

Prior to Rudakubana's sentencing last year, his defence lawyer told the court no psychiatric evidence could suggest a mental disorder contributed to his actions.

The court also heard how Rudakubana presented as having high functioning autism and did not have any associated learning disabilities.

Stan Reiz KC added that his client had appeared to have been a "normal child" until he reached 13, adding: "However, he did make a transition from a normal, well-disciplined child to someone who was capable of committing acts of such shocking and senseless violence."

Rudakubana was deemed mentally fit to be detained, interviewed and stand trial. His late guilty plea meant his mental health was not discussed in detail in court during a trial.

He was given a 52-year prison sentence in January 2025 but the judge was unable to impose a whole life order due to Rudakubana being 17 when he carried out the attack. He will likely never be released.

News.title: Mega dinghy carries record 165 migrants to UK
News.content:
A record 165 migrants reached the UK in a single boat, the Home Office has confirmed.

The number broke the previous record from July, when 128 crossed the Channel from France in one vessel.

Border Security Command was pictured towing a mega dinghy - estimated to be the same size as a standard bus at 13m (42ft) long - when it arrived in Dover on Thursday afternoon.

A Home Office spokesperson said the crossing served as a "stark reminder that criminal gangs have no regard for the safety of those they claim to help".

"The reality is clear and lives are being lost in the Channel," they added.

A total of 162 people died, external in the busy waterway between 2018 and 2025, according to the University of Oxford's Migration Observatory.

This rises to 257 when considering other migration-related deaths in the area, such as accidents involving people trying to board lorries bound for the UK, it added.

News.title: Dad who murdered four-week-old son jailed for 18 years
News.content:
A man who murdered his four-week-old son after drinking up to nine pints of beer on a night out has been jailed for life with a minimum term of 18 years.

Tony Bartlett returned to the family home in Chard, Somerset, on 16 July 2022 and shook baby Atticus in what the sentencing judge described as "a sudden fit of anger".

The 39-year-old caused serious injuries to his son's spinal cord and ribs, as well as brain damage so severe he never regained consciousness or the ability to breathe independently. Atticus died seven days later.

Bartlett, who was convicted after a trial at Bristol Crown Court earlier this month, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 18 years.

Warning: This story contains details which readers may find distressing.

The trial heard the former postman, from Axminster in Devon, had gone to a pub and comedy club with his then-partner Evelyn Ballentyne on the night Atticus was fatally injured.

It was their first evening out since their son's birth.

After they returned home, Ballentyne went upstairs and left Bartlett alone to feed Atticus.

News.title: Fifty women tell BBC they were pressured into having sex with strangers
News.content:
Warning: This story contains details of sexual acts

Fifty women have told the BBC they were pressured or coerced by their partners into having sex with strangers.

They got in contact following an investigation which told the story of a woman who said she had been pressured into having sex with more than 100 people she did not know.

Many of the women who came forward said they had sex through swinging despite not wanting to, either because they feared the consequences of refusing or felt they had to keep their partners happy.

They spoke of deep, long-lasting trauma.

"I remember many nights of my partner keeping me up all night screaming at me, threatening me, and attempting to gaslight me into believing this was something I wanted," said one woman. "It was never what I wanted."

Another told us: "I felt like I had been given away. I felt used. I felt so dirty."

Most encounters were arranged via the website FabSwingers, say the women, which claims to have more than half a million UK active monthly accounts.

Six women told BBC News they had been raped by men met through the site.

One said her partner had forced her to have sex with more than 90 men through FabSwingers. On one occasion, he held her down by the ankles, she told us.

Sixteen said intimate photos of them had been uploaded to the website without their permission.

News.title: Sarah Ferguson's charity formally closes down
News.content:
Sarah Ferguson's charity, Sarah's Trust, has formally wound up and is marked as "removed" on the public register of charities.

The charity said in February it would close "for the foreseeable future" days after new details emerged about the former Duchess of York's friendship with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Among more than three million documents released by the US Department of Justice (DoJ) earlier this year were emails appearing to show Ferguson was in contact with Epstein while he was in prison for soliciting sex from a minor. Being named in the documents does not indicate wrongdoing.

The BBC has contacted Ferguson's representatives for comment on the closure of her charity.

Established in 2020, Sarah's Trust was "dedicated to supporting frontline, grassroots work to address the humanitarian and environmental crisis, the hunger crisis and issues perpetuating cycles of extreme poverty", according to its website.

In February, a spokesperson for the foundation said the decision to close had come after "some months" of discussion.

The foundation did not provide further details behind its decision to close at the time.

The massive drop of files by the DoJ earlier this year suggested Ferguson had been closer to Epstein than previously thought.

In the files, Ferguson was seen praising the late sex offender in 2009 as "the brother I have always wished for".

The emails also suggest she took her daughters along for lunch with him in Miami, days after his release from prison.

Ferguson's representatives have not responded to previous requests for comment on the documents.

The former duchess has already been dropped by multiple charities over her Epstein links.

In October, she lost her duchess title when her ex-husband, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, relinquished his Duke of York title over his links with Epstein, and she was also forced to move out of his Windsor mansion, Royal Lodge, where the couple lived together, despite having divorced in 1996.

News.title: Nine men in court over historical child sexual exploitation offences
News.content:
Nine men have appeared in court charged with a total of 41 historical sexual offences, relating to eight victims who were children at the time.

The men, aged between 54 and 76, were arrested in Newport, Swansea, London, Birmingham, Lancashire, Edinburgh and the Argyll and Bute area of Scotland earlier in July.

Gwent Police initiated Operation Oak after several women reported the abuse, which took place in south Wales between 1985 and 1996.

Appearing at Newport Magistrates' Court, the defendants were told most charges were so serious that the cases would be transferred to Crown court.

The men, who are all British citizens, were granted bail. They will appear at Cardiff Crown Court on 21 August.

Operation Oak has been described by the force as a "complex and long-running investigation into group-based child sexual exploitation in south Wales".

Many of the charges relate to the rape of children.

No pleas were entered during the short hearings at Newport Magistrates' Court on Friday.

The defendants spoke only to confirm their names, dates of birth and addresses. One appeared via video-link.

Beijing announced Friday that China's top police chief and the director of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation have committed to enhancing law enforcement cooperation following their meeting in the Chinese capital.

During talks with FBI Director Kash Patel, China's Minister of Public Security, Wang Xiaohong, stated that both sides should "engage in more constructive dialogue on the basis of mutual respect and deepen practical cooperation" against a range of criminal activities, an official Chinese summary showed.

Their meeting followed two recent repatriations of fugitives between China and the United States, which do not share an extradition treaty.

Patel said on X that he welcomed the direct engagements with Chinese public security officials, which he said has produced results in shutting off fentanyl precursor pipelines and expanding joint efforts on scam centers, violent crimes against children and a fugitive task force.

On Thursday, China's Public Security Ministry said it had handed over to U.S. law enforcement authorities a U.S. fugitive wanted for serious violent crimes, including the suspected murder of a spouse and the sexual assault of a young girl.

( Reuters )

Chinese and U.S. law enforcement agencies have recently carried out "a series of practical cooperation in areas such as counter-narcotics, repatriation of illegal immigrants, fugitive recovery, combating telecom and cyber fraud, and anti-money laundering", the ministry said.

It added that such cooperation was in line with a consensus reached between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Days earlier, the U.S. repatriated to Beijing a fugitive accused of kidnapping and killing Chinese citizens overseas, Chinese state media said. The repatriation was hailed by Beijing as "the latest achievement" in implementing the presidents' consensus.

The FBI's Patel visited Beijing in November 2025 to discuss fentanyl and law enforcement issues, following a summit in October of that year between Trump and Xi, when the two leaders agreed on cooperation to fight fentanyl trafficking, Reuters reported.

The two presidents are set to meet again in Washington in September, Trump has said.

A'Zariah Miles' dream of attending Howard University was a few weeks from being realized. Then it all came crashing down.

Miles, 17, of Knoxville, Tennessee, is one of more than 500 incoming first-year students at Howard who learned this week that they have been unenrolled from the prestigious, historically Black Washington, D.C., university and no longer have spots for the upcoming fall semester that begins Aug. 17.

Many have taken to social media — some in tears — to share their stories. Some posts have gone viral.

After Miles learned she had been unenrolled, her mother, Kendra Miles, said the school's automated system would not allow the family to enroll in a payment plan because the amount that was owed made them ineligible to sign up.

“I’ve reached out since we got the email (Wednesday). I've emailed, literally, everybody," Kendra Miles said. “I emailed her adviser. He responded and said it wasn't a mistake and there was nothing they could do.”

On Friday, Howard confirmed in an email that the school sent notifications to “502 first-time-in-college students whose accounts did not reflect the required enrollment and financial obligations by the previously communicated deadlines."

Starting in March, the unenrolled students began receiving specific communications about enrollment requirements, payment expectations and deadlines via email and orientation sessions, the school said.

“The university recognizes that timing differences may have occurred between when financial aid was reflected and when charges were finalized,” Howard said in the email. “Students who believe their account did not accurately reflect their financial standing at the deadline should contact the Bursar’s Office. Each case will be reviewed individually to determine whether adjustments or reinstatement are appropriate.”

Howard, one of about 100 historically Black colleges and universities in the United States, had an undergraduate enrollment last fall of about 11,000. The average annual tuition for undergraduate students living on campus is about $38,000. Housing costs are about $13,600.

Laverne Mickens coaches students and their families on how to apply for college scholarships. Mickens said that she answered more than 400 emails Wednesday and Thursday from students and families impacted by the enrollment situation at Howard. She said most of them were strangers and they were “frantic and crying.”

“People are devastated,” said Mickens who runs The Scholarship College Mama LLC, which is not affiliated with Howard. “Parents are saying: ‘Can you help us? Howard unenrolled us.’ ”

A'Zariah Miles, who plans to major in biology, chose Howard over other schools that accepted her. Now, she is worried that it is too deep into the summer to enroll elsewhere.

“Everybody’s housing is booked, or I can’t enroll because it’s too late or I missed orientation,” she said. “I've been trying to continue to have hope with Howard, but I don't really have that much time before school starts and I don't really want to have a gap year.”

Like Miles and others, Saniah Collins learned Wednesday that she no longer was enrolled at Howard.

“My mom is part of a parent group chat,” said Collins, 17, of Atlanta. “That day we learned that a lot of students were getting unenrolled."

Collins received an email from the school Wednesday afternoon that said a July 10 deadline to pay her tuition balance or make payment arrangements had passed and the school no longer could hold her place.

But Collins said she was also told by an adviser that most of her balance for the fall semester was paid. She's not giving up.

“I worked like crazy to get into this school,” Collins said. “Howard has been my everything. My whole senior year, my whole summer I worked consistently on scholarships. We tried to make ourselves 10 steps ahead to make sure we were on the right page.”

___

Williams is as member of AP’s Race & Ethnicity team. He reported from Detroit.

Tom Johnstone and Lachlan Walmsley scored doubles as 12-man Wakefield ran in nine tries to demolish shell-shocked West Yorkshire derby rivals Castleford 52-14.

The hosts looked to be in trouble at the DIY Kitchens Stadium when they trailed 10-6 after Matty Storton’s early dismissal, but they turned in a rampant display to clinch a sixth successive Super League win.

Wakefield were ahead inside 45 seconds of kick-off when Johnstone found space down the left and drew his man before slipping the ball inside to Storton to cross before Max Jowitt added the conversion.

Cas had to fight for their lives amid an early onslaught, but they were back in it with 16 minutes played when Tom Weaver pounced after a deflected grubber kick fell nicely into his path, the half-back converting his own try to make it 6-6.

The Tigers’ evening took a further turn for the better within six minutes when Storton was dismissed for a high tackle on Alex Mellor, and they swiftly made their numerical advantage count when winger Jason Qareqare blasted his way over in the left corner.

However, Trinity were back in front on the half-hour when replacement Caius Faatili forced his way over and Jowitt added the two points before himself darting over from dummy half and converting his own score to make it 18-10 at the break.

Wakefield extended their lead further within three minutes of the restart when Isaiah Vagana collected Jake Trueman’s lofted kick and exchanged passes with Cameron Scott before touching down, and Johnstone snatched a quick-fire double with Jowitt adding all three kicks to leave the score at 36-10.

Corey Hall muscled his way over the line and Walmsley added his name to the scoresheet after Vagana had tapped down Trueman’s up and under before doubling his tally after Qareqare had succumbed under another aerial assault from Truman, Jowitt taking his tally to 20 points before Qaraqare’s late consolation try.

Asked about his side’s end-of-season prospects, Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell told Sky Sports: “We just keep ticking along and doing our jobs, stay consistent – we’ve got a tough away trip at Catalans next week – just keep doing what we’re doing, don’t get too carried away.

“We’ve been saying that, but I think we should be excited as a team. We play some smart stuff and the boys are tuned in with each other. It’s a pleasure to play the game when you feel like that – I remember those times – and as a coach, you’ve got a team you can trust, which is awesome.”

Disappointed opposite number Ryan Carr said: “How we started the game is how we wanted to play the game, and then we didn’t touch the ball for the next 65 minutes pretty much after that through our own doing.

“Unfortunately, you can’t win if you don’t have the ball, and you won’t have the ball unless you want to make tackles. It’s a simple game.”

Police Scotland has declared a major incident as emergency services continue to battle a significant wildfire raging through the Cairngorms National Park.

The blaze's behaviour has become increasingly unpredictable, exacerbated by warnings of drastically changed weather conditions, including stronger winds.

As a precautionary measure, homes around Nethy Bridge have been evacuated, with residents directed to a dedicated respite centre at the Macdonald Aviemore Hotel.

Access roads leading into Nethy Bridge are now closed to the public.

Superintendent Judy Hill said: “The weather conditions experienced within the Cairngorms over the last 24 hours have added further complexities to this situation.

“With evidence suggesting the fire is spreading towards Nethy Bridge, the decision has been taken to declare a major incident and evacuate residents as a precaution.

open image in gallery Homes around Nethy Bridge have been evacuated ( Ryan McDougall/PA )

“Additional police resources are being deployed to assist in contacting those who need to leave their properties and to maintain cordons around restricted areas while our fire service colleagues continue to tackle the wildfire.

“We understand this is a very concerning time for residents, businesses and visitors to the Cairngorms region.

“Please be assured that the multi-agency response remains fully committed to bringing this incident to a safe conclusion as quickly as possible.”

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) said it has maintained a “significant operational response” since the wildfire was first reported on July 15.

More than 500 firefighters have tackled the blaze over the last nine days, alongside specialist wildfire appliances, all-terrain vehicles, helicopter water-bombing operations and partner agencies.

Deputy assistant chief officer Kenny Barbour said: “Our firefighters, specialist resources and partners have worked tirelessly over the past nine days to respond to this challenging and complex wildfire incident.

“The combination of prolonged dry conditions, strengthening winds and challenging terrain has created an extremely complex operational environment.

“Large areas of the fire ground are inaccessible by vehicle or on foot, making helicopter water-bombing operations and specialist wildfire tactics essential to our response.”

open image in gallery More than 500 firefighters have tackled the blaze over the last nine days ( PA )

He added: “We recognise this is an extremely worrying time for those affected, particularly residents who have been asked to leave their homes. Public safety remains our absolute priority, and we ask everyone to continue following the advice of Police Scotland and to stay away from the affected areas while firefighting operations remain ongoing.”

Members of the public are asked to avoid the affected areas within the Cairngorms National Park. The SFRS said the area remains unsafe due to active firefighting operations, rapidly changing fire conditions and helicopter activity.

First Minister John Swinney urged people to respect the exclusion zones around the fire.

He told the Press Association: “I would obviously ask people in the region to follow all of the advice that is available and to respect the exclusion zone that’s been put in place.

“This is an incident that we felt was moving in a positive direction earlier this week, but with the change of weather circumstances – which is an illustration of just the scale and difficulty of the situation that we are managing – it has moved in the other direction.”

His comments came as smoke from the ongoing wildfire near Glenmore drifted as far as Aberdeen due to changing wind conditions.

The wildfire, which broke out near the village of Glenmore on Wednesday last week, led to residents and campsites being evacuated.

It covered an area of about six square kilometres of heather and small trees at its height.

News.content:

California's recent June primary saw nearly 150,000 mail-in ballots rejected, marking a significant surge from previous elections, despite the state's ongoing efforts to simplify voting and boost participation.

This substantial increase underscores persistent challenges within the state's electoral process, which has long been criticized for its ponderously slow vote counts that can drag on for weeks.

The state has implemented various measures aimed at making voting more accessible, including the automatic mailing of ballots to every registered voter.

These mail-in ballots are designed to be counted even if they arrive up to seven days after Election Day, provided they bear a postmark from the election date.

Yet, according to data from the secretary of state's office, the primary driver behind the heightened rejection numbers is late arrival. Voting experts suspect the core issue lies with postmarks applied after Election Day, rendering these ballots ineligible for tabulation.

Changes within the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) are increasingly believed to be a contributing factor to the timing of when these crucial postmarks are applied.

In the June election, 148,241 mail ballots were ultimately rejected, representing 1.73% of all mail ballots cast.

This figure marks an increase from the 108,982 mail ballots rejected in the 2024 primary, which had a 1.56% rejection rate.

( Getty )

In 2022, 105,818 mail ballots were voided during the primary, with a rate similar to that of the 2024 primary. Lateness alone accounted for a staggering 93,479 rejected ballots in June, making it by far the largest category for disqualification.

This number is up from approximately 70,000 in the 2022 primary and 76,000 in the 2024 primary, though turnout in those earlier elections was comparatively smaller.

Kim Alexander, president of the nonpartisan California Voter Foundation, expressed significant concern over the jump in late rejections.

She suggested this, alongside evolving postal procedures, might be linked to a late surge in ballots as many voters delayed their decisions in a competitive gubernatorial race.

Alexander stated, "Ballots rejected due to lateness are caused primarily to being postmarked too late to count, not because they arrived too late to count."

Mindy Romero, director of the Center for Inclusive Democracy, added that the growing number of late rejections "does really demand the question why this is happening," prompting a closer examination of the underlying causes.

Lawmakers have also voiced concerns regarding USPS changes. In January, a group of predominantly Democratic U.S. senators wrote to the Postal Service, alarmed that mail-processing alterations could impact postmark dates during a crucial election year that will determine control of Congress.

An updated agency policy indicates that postmarks might reflect the day mail is handled at a processing center, rather than the day it was initially received.

With recent consolidations, these centers are often further from certain communities, potentially exacerbating delays. In a related development, two Wisconsin Democrats, U.S. Sen. Tammy Baldwin and Gov. Tony Evers, called on the Postal Service in April to address delays that caused hundreds of ballots to arrive after Election Day in their state.

Earlier this year, California election officials had already urged voters to mail ballots early, citing potential USPS service slowdowns.

Beyond lateness, nearly 44,000 ballots were rejected due to mismatched signatures, while over 8,300 lacked any signature on the returned envelope.

Other reasons included voters having already cast a ballot (743 cases), a ballot being missing from the return envelope, or multiple ballots sent back in a single envelope.

The data did not provide a breakdown of these uncounted ballots by party registration. Geographically, Tulare County, located in the agriculture-heavy Central Valley, recorded the highest mail ballot rejection rate in June at 3.52%.

It was followed by Alpine County, south of Lake Tahoe, and Merced County, also in the Central Valley, both at 3.36%.

California's reputation for slow vote tabulation contrasts sharply with states like Florida and Texas, which quickly finalize their counts. Donald Trump has previously leveraged California’s protracted counting to criticize the state’s elections, and his Department of Justice launched an investigation into Los Angeles County’s elections.

In June, a federal judge halted an executive order by Donald Trump that aimed to create a federal voter list and restrict mail ballot eligibility. Despite these controversies, mail voting has gained bipartisan popularity, and a 2025 report by the Brookings Institution found mail voting fraud to be minuscule, with approximately four cases per 10 million mail ballots, suggesting that the integrity of the system remains largely intact despite the operational challenges.

Universal Orlando is seeing a slower-than-expected summer at its theme parks, according to parent company Comcast.

During a Thursday earnings call, company executives said attendance at the Orlando parks has been “softening” since June and has continued to trend lower into the third quarter. Comcast admitted the slowdown resulted in performance that was "below expectations."

Comcast co-CEO Mike Cavanagh cited surging gas prices as a possible factor behind weaker-than-expected performance. The average U.S. gas price is $4.10, up from $3.16 a year ago, as President Donald Trump’s war with Iran continues to choke off oil supply.

"We believe there are some temporary factors at work, including higher fuel prices and weaker consumer sentiment, but we are watching these trends closely," Cavanagh said on the call, Fox 35 Orlando reports.

Executives did not share specific attendance figures, the outlet reports, but they did highlight the early success of Epic Universe.

open image in gallery Higher fuel prices may be contributing to slower attendance at Universal Orlando this summer, Comcast executives said ( Universal Orlando )

Epic Universe opened in May 2025 with five themed areas: Celestial Park, Dark Universe, How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk, Super Nintendo World, and The Wizarding World of Harry Potter – Ministry of Magic.

"Epic Universe continues to perform well and is delivering the strong guest response we expected," Cavanagh said.

Even amid the recent attendance slowdown, executives said they remain confident in Universal’s theme park future.

Executives on the call also pointed to the recently opened Universal Kids Resort in Texas and a planned resort in the United Kingdom.

"We have great brands, great locations and a proven playbook for investing behind attractions and experiences that create real consumer demand and strong returns,” Cavanagh said.

open image in gallery Earlier this month, Universal Orlando rolled out a major deal for Florida residents, offering unlimited park visits through the end of the year ( Getty Images/iStock )

Universal’s parks business saw a small boost in revenue this spring, bringing in $2.4 billion in the second quarter, up 2.7 percent from last year. The company said much of that growth came from the success of Epic Universe, according to Fox 35 Orlando.

However, higher costs ate into profits, with the parks division’s earnings falling 5.1 percent to $609 million compared with the same period last year.

Despite the dip in attendance, Universal has plenty on the horizon. Construction is underway on Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift, a new roller coaster coming to Universal Studios Florida in 2027. Meanwhile, a recently filed permit has sparked speculation that a Zelda or Pokémon attraction could be coming to Islands of Adventure.

Universal Orlando is also expanding its dining lineup at CityWalk, with new spots such as Five Guys, Luke Combs’ Category 10 and Joey Fatone’s Fat One’s Hot Dogs and Italian Ice on the way, Fox 35 Orlando reports.

Earlier this month, Universal Orlando announced it is offering Florida residents a discounted unlimited-access ticket, allowing visits to Universal Studios Florida and Islands of Adventure through December. The “2-Park Unlimited Days Park-to-Park” ticket costs $199 before tax, just slightly more than a single-day two-park ticket.

News.title: Britain to pay higher Trump tariffs than EU
News.content:
Britain will pay higher tariffs than the EU after Donald Trump’s latest global trade onslaught.

Bosses in Britain have warned they will lose any competitive advantage over the bloc after the US President announced higher import taxes on goods from 60 trading partners.

The US administration imposed 10pc tariffs on both Britain and the EU to replace levies which expired overnight following a Supreme Court ruling earlier this year.

Britain must pay the import taxes on top of so-called Most Favoured Nation tariffs imposed on all members of the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

However, from Friday, the EU’s tariffs are inclusive of the WTO levies. The average WTO tariff rate is between 2.4pc to 3.5pc for non-agricultural food products.

William Bain, head of trade policy at the BCC, said: “There will be concerns about the loss of the UK’s competitive advantage over the EU and other countries which have secured a more favourable deal in other goods sectors.”

A government spokesman said: “There is no negative ‌change ‌to ⁠the tariff rate facing UK businesses as a result of this ⁠announcement.”

“Our agreement with the US remains in place, and today we see ​an improvement to our ‌trading terms with zero tariffs on whisky and medical technology.”

Jonathan Reynolds, the Business Secretary, said Scottish whisky distilleries would get a “boost” from the new tariff regime, which removes levies on scotch under a deal first announced during the King’s state visit to the US in April.

On Friday, Trump also threatened new tariffs on the European Union in response to billions worth of fines imposed on US tech giants by competition regulators.

In a post on his social media platform Truth Social, Trump said: “The United States of America is not a “PIGGYBANK” for Europe, nor will we allow it to be!”

The US president said he expected to impose “substantial tariffs” on the EU after the European Commission fined Google €890m (£760m) on Thursday.

UK and European stock markets shrugged off the latest tariffs, with the FTSE 100 up 0.9pc.

However, Wall Street was more mixed. The S&P 500 was roughly flat, while the Nasdaq Composite was down 1.1pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.3pc near the end of Friday’s trading session.

It followed dramatic falls in Asia overnight, with Japan’s Nikkei falling 2.7pc and South Korea’s Kospi down 5.7pc.

News.title: Mason Mount offering Michael Carrick a midfield solution which could have legs
News.content:
It is not uncommon to hear football club executives talking about the importance of the “money being on the pitch”.

In other words, managers having their best players fit and available most if not all of the time. Quality at the top level is essential but so is robustness. They go hand in hand.

Unfortunately for Manchester United, the money has not been on the pitch down the years nearly as much as the club would want or expect.

Bruno Fernandes stands out for what he does with the ball primarily, but also because he plays almost every minute of every game and, while his sheer indefatigability is extreme, United know they need more of his ilk.

This is why the forthcoming season is such a big one for Mason Mount. His quality has seldom been in doubt. The problem is he has rarely been on the pitch long or consistently enough to show it.

Indeed, the one-time England midfielder has started just 25 Premier League matches since his £60m move from Chelsea three years ago and that perennial unavailability is one of the reasons doubts were being cast about his Old Trafford future going into this summer.

Yet Michael Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and intriguingly the 27-year-old could yet have an impact on what the club do during the remaining six weeks of the transfer window.

For the second time in the space of six days, Mount was deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside new £48m, signing Andrey Santos for Friday’s resounding 5-0 victory over Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim, just as he had done against Wrexham last weekend.

News.title: Eleanor Cardwell: ‘Comfortable sportswear should not be expensive’
News.content:
What sports shoes do you recommend?

Robert, South West

The sports shoes that I’m currently wearing are from Puma. They’re very comfortable and have support. I actually wear a basketball shoe at the minute to have more support up the ankle.

A lot of the girls wear Asics as well, which I know is the netball shoe. I’ve worn Puma for the last four years, so I would recommend them.

But honestly, whatever works best for you, you have to try them out. Whatever is best for your instep and whatever is comfiest. And if you need more ankle support, you can put some ankle braces on.

How has playing for Manchester Thunder helped you develop as a player?

Jason, London

Manchester has massively helped me develop as a player. I’ve been playing here since 2012. As a young girl, it created me as a person, to be honest with you. It’s such a family environment that I think a lot of my values come from this club. So my family values, being connected, creating energy – all those things come rooted from this club, which is incredible.

I think whatever step you are in your career, whether you’re a young athlete or senior, they help you develop. Even now I’m 31, they’re still helping me learn new things on the court. The coaches are incredible, and I’m constantly learning and being inspired by them every single week.

Do players retire from elite netball quite young?

Helen, South West

I think it depends on the athlete. Some can retire at 40, and that’s because their bodies are so conditioned, and they might not have had any major injuries in their career. They’re able to continue to push themselves all the way until 40.

But I’d say the average is probably mid-30s. Now the Super League has become professional, the younger athletes are getting better training from a younger age. We want to keep pushing ourselves to play as long as possible.

How can netball get more coverage when women’s football is constantly pushed?

Sarah, South West

I think netball needs to have more sponsors to get more media coverage. Bigger sponsors.

Players need to put their personalities more out there on social media, so brands will want to work with us. Everyone’s got amazing personalities in netball. They [brands] should want to be a part of the netball players’ stories and the netball teams.

But it’s about getting as much exposure as possible, and making sure that everyone is going on YouTube or BBC, so more people are able to learn about the sport.

I loved netball at school. How do I get involved now in my 60s?

Sue, Yorkshire

Netball is for everyone. I personally love going to walking netball sessions and taking them through classes. You can go to the England Netball website and find out where you can play locally.

There’s also Back to Netball, depending on your ability and what you want to get out of it. Personally, I think walking netball is so much fun. The women who are in those sessions are a huge laugh, and I know when I retire, I’m going to be joining a group, for sure.

Apart from netball, what other hobbies do you have? How do they help you relieve the pressure of competition?

George, London

I feel like over the past few years I’ve really got into some new hobbies. I love reading. I love fantasy reading, like Throne of Glass. I love BookTok, so I’ve really got into that.

I’m also very crafty. I like making things – I’ve made little crochet bees for all the girls, and I like drawing, and painting occasionally – just wholesome activities to take me away from netball life. As soon as I zone in on an activity, I’m locked in and I have to complete it.

News.title: Africa improves health defences, but it remains vulnerable to pandemics
News.content:
Africa is significantly better prepared for a pandemic than it was five years ago, a major review of the continent’s health security has found.

The review, which tracked dozens of health metrics across the continent, found that local and international investments in Africa’s health sector since the pandemic have “paid off.”

Published by the Brown University Pandemic Centre and the Nuclear Threat Initiative, a US non-profit, the report is the third of its kind and provides an update on two previous reviews from 2019 and 2021.

Investment in health by African governments grew rapidly during the pandemic. Post-pandemic, the average spend now sits at around 7.4 per cent of GDP, roughly $135 billion per year across the continent.

That figure still falls significantly below those of high-income countries, where the average spend on health sits at around 11.2 per cent of GDP.

The new African Health Security Index report found that almost every African country – 53 out of 54, excluding only the Republic of the Congo – has improved its ability to prevent, detect, and respond to disease outbreaks since 2021, the last time the index was updated.

Overall, the continent scores 41.2 out of 100 on its health security – up from 32.9 five years ago.

The score is built from hundreds of specific indicators covering things like how far people live from a hospital, how well infectious patients can be isolated, the size and training level of the health workforce, laboratory capacity, and the availability of vaccines and other critical medicines during an outbreak.

News.title: Ebola death toll passes 1,000 as outbreak shows no signs of slowing
News.content:
More than 1,000 people have now died in the outbreak of Ebola in the Congo, as medics struggle to curb the fastest-growing epidemic of the virus.

Dozens of deaths are being recorded each day and modelling has forecast that, in a worst case scenario, it could become the worst Ebola outbreak in history.

The outbreak, centred on the north east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), passed the four-figure death milestone little more than two months after it was first declared.

By contrast, the worst outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever on record, which struck West Africa from 2014 to 2016, took eight months from the first case to reach 1,000 deaths. It went on to kill 11,000 people.

The latest figures from the DRC’s national public health institute show 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 patients in isolation or hospitalised.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

Sports.title: Axed top-tier ref sues bosses over ‘bullying’ after claiming he was put in a choke-hold at a training camp
Sports.content:
REFFING DISGRACE Axed top-tier ref sues bosses over ‘bullying’ after claiming he was put in a choke-hold at a training camp

Credit: Getty

AN axed top-tier ref is suing bosses — claiming he was put in a choke-hold at a training camp.

The unnamed official loses his £100,000-a-year salary as one of five demoted from the Premier League and the Championship next season.



A source told The Sun that during an appeal process the ref raised the allegation he had been put in a choke-hold by his trainer in front of witnesses in September 2024.

He is believed to have later acknowledged it was a less aggressive incident.



But he is still suing Professional Game Match Officials Ltd — now called Pro Ref.

The source said: “The refs are promoted and demoted based on performance, and it is sad to see this action being taken.”



Meanwhile, about 35 refs were told they had to return money to the organisation after a bungle over performance pay-outs.

The source added: “There was talk of rebranding PGMOL after the downfall of Prem ref David Coote. But the rebrand couldn’t have had a worse start.”

Pro Ref said in relation to the pay bungle: “We quickly rectified a human processing error whereby a very small number of officials were initially affected either by underpayment or overpayment. All officials will receive what was agreed based on their performance in 2025/26.”

The demoted refs have lost their money-spinning jobs and guaranteed salary but can still pick up match fees next season by officiating in Leagues 1 and 2 and the National League.



Up to 15 assistant referees have been told their services will not be required next season owing to a “lack of potential”.

The organisation is accused of getting rid of refs to bring in “more diverse, younger officials”.

Sports.title: Aston Villa in transfer talks to sign £65m-rated Chelsea star Nicolas Jackson as Ollie Watkins edges towards exit
Sports.content:
ASTON VILLA have opened talks with Chelsea to sign £65million-rated Senegal striker Nicolas Jackson.

And Ollie Watkins could be on his way out of Villa Park as Fenerbahce push to land the 30-year-old England forward.



Unai Emery is determined to capture Jackson, 25, after securing Alejandro Garnacho on loan from Stamford Bridge.

New Blues boss Xabi Alonso wants to assess Jackson during pre-season, though the Senegalese star is not part of the initial squad which set off for Australia today.



Jackson is still on holiday having made it to the last-32 of the World Cup this summer.

However, defender Jorrel Hato, 20, who reached the same stage with Holland, is on the plane with the Chelsea squad.

Jackson scored three goals in 27 appearances at Villarreal after Emery gave him his debut.

He previously said of Villa boss Emery: “Unai taught me everything.”

Villa would have to sign Jackson on a permanent deal as Premier League rules do not permit clubs to take two players on loan from another top-flight club.

The Europa League winners have to clear all of their transfer incomings past Uefa as part of a ‘settlement agreement’ for breaching squad cost ratio rules, which limit clubs to spending 70 per cent of revenue on salaries and fees.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Uefa financial rules do not allow clubs to book the full profit on transactions considered ‘swaps’ within a 45-day period, which this deal would fall under after Morgan Rogers’ £117m move from Villa Park to Stamford Bridge.

But the Rogers deal can aid Villa’s accounting because clubs who have sold a player can book the entire value of the sale on one season’s accounts.

Whereas if you are a buying club, the cost of any transfer fee can be spread across the length of a contract.

Jackson made a loan move to Bayern Munich last summer, but the Bundesliga champions opted against keeping him.



Watkins has two years left on his Villa deal and Fenerbahce are trying to tempt him with big money.

The former Brentford man has scored 108 goals in 278 appearances for the club.

Sports.title: Man City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma marries wife Alessia in lavish ceremony with Haaland and wag in attendance
Sports.content:

The Manchester City goalkeeper tied the knot with childhood sweetheart Alessia Elefante in Chiesa Madre di San Giorgio Martire in Locorotondo, Italy.



He met the interior designer back in 2016 in their hometown of Castellammare di Stabia, near Naples. They also had their son, Leo, in 2024.

They announced their engagement in May with the Instagram post that read: “Long-term contract signed.”



Names like Pep Guardiola, Erling Haaland, Sandro Tonali, Paolo Maldini and Nicolò Barella were present at the ceremony.

Ironically, Maldini and Guardiola have already been in talks this week to discuss managing the Italy national team.

However, Guardiola has decided to spend more time with his family before making his next managerial move. Andrea Pirlo is now in line for the role.

Donnarumma’s team-mate Haaland was flanked by his girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen.

The Norwegian has been enjoying himself since the World Cup where he gained a cult following in the United States.

During Norway‘s run to the quarter-finals, Haaland amassed 32.1 million new followers on social media.

He has since been enjoying himself on holiday in Italy where he and his partner were seen clubbing earlier this week.
