Sports.title: Man Utd player ratings: Joshua Zirkzee fights way back into first-team contention as Shea Lacey puts in mature display
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED’S wonderkids stole the spotlight as Michael Carrick’s side cruised to a 5-0 pre-season win over Rosenborg in Norway.

With the likes of Bruno Fernandes, Amad Diallo and Senne Lammens all absent following their World Cup commitments, it was United’s academy stars who lit up Trondheim with four debut senior goals.



Carrick’s youngsters took full advantage as Shea Lacey, Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams all found the net, while Joshua Zirkzee produced a stunning solo strike.

United continued their preparations without the bulk of their World Cup stars, but the next generation showed they are ready to stake their claim ahead of the new campaign.



Fifteen-year-old sensation JJ Gabriel was an unused substitute after dominating the build-up to the game, with Carrick opting not to hand the academy prodigy his senior bow just yet.

Here are Man Utd reporter Katherine Walsh’s match ratings for the first- and second-half XIs…

FIRST HALF

Radek Vitek – 6

The Czech keeper is hunting for a summer exit—whether on loan or permanently—but had zero chance to advertise his talents on an afternoon where he was left with virtually nothing to do.

Leny Yoro – 7

Back out of position at right-back, the French starlet again was solid in the unfamiliar role.



Is Yoro United’s new aerial threat with Casemiro gone? It looked that way when his glancing header smacked off the crossbar on the stroke of half time.

Harry Maguire – 7

Enjoyed a quiet half and was on hand with several brilliant passes through the lines.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Ayden Heaven – 7



Michael Carrick is preparing to hand Heaven a starting spot in defence on opening day, following Lisandro Martinez’s injury in the World Cup final.

The 19-year-old’s best moment came when he intercepted a Rosenborg attack in the box with a well-timed read.

Luke Shaw – 7

Looked lean and lively. Comfortable in possession and strong in the challenge,

Should have offered more in the final third, especially when United piled on the pressure.



Andrey Santos – 8

Another physical 45 minutes and could have had an assist when he delivered a one-time pass into Patrick Dorgu inside the box.

Despite it being his second match, Santos was extremely vocal in the midfield. A clear leader.

Mason Mount – 8

Back in central midfield with plenty of crisp movement and passing between him and Santos.



His link up play with Joshua Zirkzee improved on Wrexham and he closed the space on Rosenborg.

Shea Lacey – 8

Mature beyond his years. It won’t count in the official record books, but his first senior strike was pure class—cutting inside from the right to bury his signature finish.

The 19-year-old was the only academy player on the teamsheet and he didn’t look out of place as the No10.



Patrick Dorgu – 7

Tried to get forward as much as possible on the left wing. He doesn’t have Marcus Rashford‘s feet but Dorgu was involved in good chemistry with Mount and Zirkzee.

Bryan Mbeumo – 7

Looked sharper than he did against Wrexham, treating the near empty ground to a sublime nutmeg and a well-placed cross from a free-kick that Yoro smacked off the woodwork.

He overhit a cross into Lacey before that, but the Cameroonian found some rhythm.



Joshua Zirkzee – 8

Night and day from the Wrexham display. Capitalising on Sesko’s absence, he backed up his promise to fight for his place.

On top of setting up Lacey’s opener and linking brilliantly with Mbeumo, he netted an outrageous solo goal—driving forward and dummying past two defenders and the keeper. Dropped deep in midfield.



SECOND HALF

Jaydan Kamason (replaced Harry Maguire, 45′) – 8

The full-back was a like-for-like change with Shaw and performed brilliantly. Two top level and skilful assists for Amass and Ethan Williams.

Harry Amass (replaced Luke Shaw, 45′) – 8

Involved in a gorgeous delayed one-two with Zirkzee for 2-0. He scored a back post tap in and should be around the first team this season with Shaw the only out-and-out left back in a busier schedule.

Tyler Fletcher (replaced Shea Lacey, 61′) – 6



Lost his man a couple of times but recovered well. Circulated the ball well in possession.

Jacob Devaney (replaced Mason Mount, 61′) – 7

Will be delighted with a first senior goal as he hooked in a corner, albeit unofficial in the record books. He came on at centre-back again; I’m not sure he’s tall enough for it to be permanent.

Ethan Williams (replaced Bryan Mbeumo, 61′) – 7

He adjusted his body to turn Kamason’s cross home to add further gloss to a one-sided score line.



Dan Armer (replaced Leny Yoro, 61′) – 6

The corner hit off Armer as it dropped to his centre-back pair Devaney for 3-0.

Toby Collyer (replaced Andrey Santos, 61′) – 6

Sports.title: Argentina given AUTOMATIC spot in World Cup 2030 after never-before-seen Fifa decision
Sports.content:
ARGENTINA have already bagged their place in the 2030 World Cup – thanks to being in line to host just ONE clash at the tournament.

Lionel Messi and Co agonisingly missed out on winning this summer’s extravaganza as they suffered an extra-time defeat to Spain in the final.



But Argentina, who sensationally held a bus parade through Buenos Aires after being beaten, have been handed a boost ahead of the next World Cup.

They will not have to go through a gruelling qualification campaign thanks to a never-before-seen Fifa decision to have SIX co-hosts.



The majority of the showdowns will be held in Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

But Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay are also set to have one match each on their shores – giving them automatic qualification.



The three South American nations will be co-hosts as the World Cup celebrates its centenary.

Argentina, who won the tournament for a third time in Qatar four years ago, are preparing to stage a showdown at River Plate’s Estadio Monumental as a reward for being a finalist in 1930.

The opening contest will be held at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo, which was used for the first-ever World Cup game.

And Paraguay, fresh from notching a shock penalty shootout win over Germany last month, are on course to have an encounter at the Estadio Osvaldo Dominguez Dibb in Asuncion.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Argentina’s passage into the World Cup will not go down well in some quarters.

More than 23 MILLION fans from around the globe have signed a petition to get La Albiceleste banned from future tournaments.

Supporters fumed at decisions going Argentina’s way as they went in search of defending their crown.

But over 80,000 Argentines have sensationally been pushing for the World Cup final to be replayed.



They claim “rigged refereeing” allowed Spain to come out on top in extra-time.

There is uncertainty over whether Messi, 39, will be involved in the 2030 World Cup.

Sports.title: Rosenborg 0 Man Utd 5: Forgotten man Joshua Zirkzee scores ‘best pre-season goal of all time’ in Red Devils rout
Sports.content:
THERE was no Bruno Fernandes, Benjamin Sesko or Amad.

With Old Trafford‘s household names left out of the spotlight, Manchester United’s hyped-up academy army didn’t just step into the vacuum in Trondheim—they stole the show.

Five goals, four of them from United’s youth ranks. All four were unofficial debut senior ‘goals’, too.



Shea Lacey, Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams all struck, either side of an outstanding Joshua Zirkzee finish as United ramped up pre-season prep.



Michael Carrick just needed to hand 15-year-old crown jewel JJ Gabriel some minutes and it would have been the perfect trip.

Gabriel’s presence in Carrick’s 25-man travelling squad felt as though it was the prelude to him becoming one of the youngest players ever to feature in a senior game for the club.

But it wasn’t to be as Continued his schedule without almost all of his World Cup players. Striker Sesko was left at home too with a shin injury.



Lacey, 19, was Fernandes for the day at No10 and his first senior strike gave United fans a front-row seat to the trademark goal Carrington regulars know by heart.

The Liverpool-born teen steadied himself, put the defenders on their heels, and bent a beauty into the far corner, running the show against a match-fit Rosenborg midfield in the heat of their own domestic season.

Against the backdrop of near silence and more seagulls than fans, Zirkzee produced a special moment as United bounced back from their 1-0 loss to Wrexham in Helsinki.

The Dutchman sold two defenders with a sumptuous fake shot, only to sit the goalkeeper down after half-time.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Carrick went against the preseason grain by only making two changes at the break, with sub Amass playing a delayed one-two with Zirkzee for the evening.

New Rosenborg manager Erik Alfred Johansson made 10 half-time changes, prioritising their fight against relegation with the club sitting just three points above the drop zone.

An hour went by before Carrick brought in eight young avengers as Dan Gore, the Fletcher twins, Toby Collyer, Dan Armer and Devaney entered the fray.

Republic of Ireland youth international Devaney, 19, tripled the lead just seconds after stepping off the bench, hooking home from a corner past the hour mark.



The ball may have hit the arm of Devaney’s centre-back partner Dan Armer, but VAR was missing.

The closest Rosenborg came was Emil Ceide meeting a low cross from the right and striking the bar with Radek Vitek stranded.

Ten minutes later, a brilliant full-back-to-full-back combination saw Amass tap in Jaydan Kamason’s exquisite delivery across the face of goal.

Kamason then delivered a perfect cross again after dancing into the touchline from the right to deliver it on a plate for Ethan Williams.

Gabriel, entering his GCSE year and United’s academy prodigy, was sent to warm-up and stole the headlines in the pre-match build up.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the Prem Under-18 player of the season will have to wait his turn. Maybe Carrick wanted to delay his exposure for another week.

He will hope for a spot in the squad against Atletico de Madrid in Sweden next week, when one World Cup star in Amad returns.

Sports.title: Five sales Man Utd MUST make in the transfer window including England star and TWO goalkeepers
Sports.content:
WITH three more signings still wanted by Manchester United, some players have to make way to make room.

United are yet to negotiate a sale this summer as Napoli’s obligation to buy Rasmus Hojlund was part of the loan agreement struck last year.



A Manuel Ugarte sale is off the cards following his serious knee injury but a few of his teammates have got a fight on their hands to remain at United beyond the transfer window.

Here are the five players who could be shown the door before the transfer window closes on September 1.



Joshua Zirkzee

Zirkzee is in limbo at United. They want to sell him and bring in a replacement but Benjamin Sesko is not match-fit and has not figured in their pre-season friendlies yet.

With Sesko recovering from a shin injury, Zirkzee has been assured of starting roles in the first pre-season games. His inclusions have been by default.

The 25-year-old’s only competitive start this calendar year was in a goalless draw at Sunderland in May – a week after Sesko aggravated his shin injury.

Zirkzee was so blunt that the following week Michael Carrick reverted to the successful strikerless formation that yielded six wins from 11 games, excluding Sesko’s two ‘super sub’ winners.

Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, Amad, Bruno Fernandes and Mason Mount could all double as a false nine and all would arguably be preferable to Zirkzee. He has scored five Premier League goals in two seasons.

United won’t get anywhere near to the £36.5million they paid for Zirkzee in 2024.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The club would require £21.9m to avoid a loss under the squad cost ratio (SCR) and sustainability and systemic resilience laws that have replaced the profitability and sustainability rules.

Returning to Italy would be logical for Zirkzee. He made a name for himself there with Bologna, the pace of Serie A is more suited to his skill set and Italian clubs are addicted to Premier League cast-offs.

Marcus Rashford

Italy and Zirkzee go hand in glove. United need a helping hand to offload Rashford permanently.

Barcelona is a no-go after they opted for Anthony Gordon and there is not a standout elite European club in need of a winger on such a high salary.

The sale of Morgan Rogers opened up a vacancy at Aston Villa, yet Rashford’s other former club chose his old United teammate Alejandro Garnacho.



Garnacho has moved to Villa Park on a season-long loan with an obligation to buy for £43m next year.

That is considerably more than the £26m option Barca had to buy Rashford and which he is still available for.

So Rashford is running out of options but it would be rash of United to reintegrate him.

He has publicly antagonised the club, be it approving of Garnacho for donning a ‘Rashford 9’ Villa shirt in an Instagram stunt or thanking the coaches at England, Barca and Villa for his World Cup call-up.

There was no mention of Rashford’s actual employers, United.



As recently as this month, Rashford reiterated his wish for a transfer after his World Cup commitments had ended.

Rashford has entered the final two years of his contract, is United’s highest-paid player but has not played for them since December 12 2024. It is a marriage of inconvenience.

The placid Carrick could ensure there is a serene return to the fold.



Carrick worked with Rashford for nearly six years as a player and a coach and United lack an out-and-out left winger, though Cunha and Patrick Dorgu have performed impressively under Carrick.

Accommodating a squad player on £325,000 a week is not aligned with Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s business model, though.

Reintegrating Rashford after he crossed former managers Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim would potentially set a dangerous precedent at United just when they are enjoying some stability.

Altay Bayindir

Even with their first and second-choice goalies on holiday, United have a packed goalkeeping department for pre-season.

Bayindir should have returned this week after his three-week post-World Cup break. He did not play for Turkey, either.



Yet the 28-year-old has not come back to United and there is little point in doing so. United have already signed a back-up ‘keeper in Karl Darlow ahead of Bayindir’s expected departure.

Figures at Carrington have spoken highly of Bayindir’s professionalism and work ethic. But it is in the interests of all parties that he gets a permanent change of scenery after three years in Manchester.

Radek Vitek

Darlow, 35, has arrived on a free and the 40-year-old Tom Heaton signed a one-year renewal to support No.1 Senne Lammens. Vitek, 22, was a regular in the Championship last season, so he cannot be at United for the upcoming season.



The Czech’s resale value has to be relatively high after he swept the board at Bristol City’s end-of-season awards.

Vitek may have to wait a while longer as Darlow, yet to be involved in training, recovers from an injury and Lammens is still on his post-World Cup holiday.

Diego Leon

There have been a laughable amount of new additions to the United first team section on the club website.

Dan Armer, Jaydan Kamason, Jim Thwaites, Jacob Devaney, Ethan Williams and the 15-year-old JJ Gabriel have been assigned first-team status on account of their pre-season participation.

The academy sextet have been involved, unlike Diego Leon. Leon, 19, seems destined to be remembered as the forgotten signing of the 2025 summer as he has not trained with the first team this calendar year.



Paraguayan Leon was introduced to United fans on the Old Trafford pitch last year and named in the pre-season tour squad.

A year on, he has made the senior matchday squad four times and the most recent was in October.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As young as Leon is, the chances of him forging a long-term career at United seem remote. United also have plenty of specialist and auxiliary left backs (Dorgu, Luke Shaw, Harry Amass, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui).

Cashing in sooner rather than later would be sensible.

Sports.content:

‌



The Turkish side are said to have been plotting a £35m bid for the England international, only for Villa to make it clear they wouldn't accept the bid.

‌



The Sun claims several clubs in England and in Europe are keen on signing Watkins this summer. Fenerbahce had been hoping to offer the 30-year-old a contract of £7.5m and £8.5m per year over a three-year deal.

‌



Although Villa clearly outlined their stance to the Turkish side, Arsenal and United are interested in signing Watkins as they look to freshen up their attack, and £40m could be enough to lure Villa into talks.

Man Utd drop clearest hint yet over Marcus Rashford's future as club bosses reach out READ MORE :

Arsenal have been left without a choice as Mikel Arteta's transfer frustrations clear READ MORE :

Arsenal are expected to sell Gabriel Jesus this summer, with the Brazilian forward attracting interest from Serie A side AC Milan and the Gunners reportedly view Watkins as an ideal replacement.

‌



As for United, Joshua Zirkzee is being linked with a return to Italy, with Juventus keen on signing the former Bologna striker, having impressed in the Serie A before his move to Old Trafford.

View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee is one player who could leave Manchester United this summer. (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Reports earlier this week claimed the Dutch international had given Juventus his seal of approval ahead of a transfer talks with United, but as things stand, there have been no club-to-club talks.

‌



AS Roma are also said to be keen on signing Zirkzee this summer, and if United do offload the 25-year-old, The Sun suggest Michael Carrick's side would then be expected to make an official approach for Watkins.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Villa are in a tricky financial situation this summer, knowing they need to sell players in order to comply with UEFA rules.

‌



United took advantage of a £35m release clause in Youri Tielemans' Villa contract to sign the Belgian international, while PSG are in talks to re-sign Lucas Digne.

Villa are set to bring in a reported £45m from those two transfers, but have signed Swiss star Johan Manzambi for a similar fee.

They've also sanctioned the sale of Morgan Rogers for a club-record sale of £117m, with Chelsea beating Arsenal to his signature.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish offered Man City lifeline by Enzo Maresca after Pep Guardiola snub
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish offered Man City lifeline by Enzo Maresca after Pep Guardiola snub

Manchester City's new manager Enzo Maresca was asked about what the future holds for Jack Grealish after the £100million man spent last season out on loan with Everton

View 2 Images Jack Grealish's future is currently up in the air (Image: Darren Staples/AFP)

Enzo Maresca has refused to shut the door on Jack Grealish remaining at Manchester City - despite expectations that the attacker would be offloaded this summer.

‌



Grealish fell out of favour at City under Maresca's predecessor, Pep Guardiola, and subsequently joined on Everton on loan. His year-long spell at Everton was curtailed by a stress fracture in his foot, leaving the 30-year-old in a difficult position heading into the off-season.

‌



City are about to embark on a new era under Maresca after Guardiola's decision to step away from the club at the end of last season.

‌



And the Italian stopped short of completely writing off Grealish making a go of it at the club he joined for £100million back in 2021.

Enzo Maresca insists Man City won't repeat what Man Utd did after Sir Alex Ferguson READ MORE :

"At the moment, he's here. He's a Man City player," Maresca said on Friday when he was asked about Grealish, who he worked with during his spell as Guardiola's assistant.

"I always said the same. In any club I join, I like to know if there are players that belong to the club. It's my duty to try to coach them. Jack is here. I have a good relation with Jack since I left. Also, we keep in touch, and the reason why is because he has a big heart and he's a very good guy. So this is the reason why. And then we see what happens."

‌



While Grealish is now officially back on City's books, he remained at Everton's Finch Farm training base after suffering the injury.

View 2 Images Jack Grealish was frozen out by Pep Guardiola (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Everton are understood to be keen on bringing Grealish back to Merseyside once he is fully fit. Grealish notched two goals and six assists for the Toffees before injuring himself against his old club, Aston Villa.

‌



Despite being frozen out by Guardiola, City's old kingpin hinted that Grealish could still have a future at the club last October. Speaking before City played Everton, Guardiola said: "I think he has a contract for one more year with us. The important thing is he is back. He is a massive influence in the Everton games. After what's happened, maybe Manchester City want him back, but I don't know.

"Many things are still going to happen. We'll see. The important thing is he is playing again, a lot of minutes. This is the standard. I'm happy, really, honestly, that he's back in, trying his best."

Sports.title: Woking chief hits out as Jermain Defoe leaves first management job after just four months
Sports.content:
Woking chief hits out as Jermain Defoe leaves first management job after just four months

Woking confirmed the shock departure of Jermain Defoe as manager of Thursday, and now the club's director of football has said more on the former Premier League and England striker's departure

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe left Woking after just four months (Image: PA)

Woking director of football, Jody Brown, has defended the club's transfer policy after Jermain Defoe's shock departure as manager. The National League side announced on Thursday that they had parted ways with the Premier League legend, who said in a statement that it was 'impossible to continue'.

‌



The 43-year-old was appointed at the end of March and guided Woking to a 10th-place finish in English football's fifth tier. The ex-England striker won two of his six games in charge and was expected to lead the Surrey club into the 2026-27 campaign.

‌



Defoe took charge of two pre-season friendlies this summer, as Woking faced non-league side Sholing before taking on Portsmouth, one of his former clubs.

‌



Argentina players ripped apart over World Cup chaos as FIFA set to take action READ MORE :

But Woking announced on Thursday evening that his tenure had come to an abrupt end. The club said: "Woking Football Club can confirm that the club and First Team Manager Jermain Defoe have mutually agreed to part ways with immediate effect.

"We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to Jermain for his contribution during his time at Woking Football Club, and we wish him every success in the future. The club remains fully focused on delivering its objectives both on and off the pitch. We would like to thank our supporters for their continued support."

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe did not last long at Woking (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

‌



Now, the club's director of football, Brown, has defended himself after being criticised on X. When one account asked if Defoe was available for an exit interview to answer a few questions, a fan replied: "I can answer them for you if you like... our director of football thinks he runs the club, calls all the shots, chose all the triallists, none of which JD wanted, and is very tight with the owner. All of which led to empty promises."

Brown then replied to the supporter's post – alleging that Defoe "led all recruitment and all triallists". He claimed: "Of the vast number of triallists, I did not choose one. Not one.

"Jermain led all recruitment and all triallists. All Jermain’s contacts, all linked to him. Every single one. Empty promises? We gave everything that was asked. Everything. I’m sure it’ll all come out in due course."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Jermain Defoe has been approached by Mirror Football for comment.

Defoe’s Woking reign got underway with an entertaining 3-3 draw with Eastleigh before victories in two of the next five fixtures. He had been preparing them for their season opener against Sutton United.

Article continues below

But his shock exit means the Cards are now searching for his successor ahead of the National League campaign, which gets underway on August 8.

The ex-Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland marksman started his coaching career as Steven Gerrard’s assistant at Rangers five years ago. Defoe then headed back to Spurs to work with their youth teams before joining Woking.

Sports.title: Shea Lacey and forgotten Man Utd star send Michael Carrick timely reminder in friendly
Sports.content:
Shea Lacey and forgotten Man Utd star send Michael Carrick timely reminder in friendly

MAN UTD 5-0 ROSENBORG: Michael Carrick's side kickstarted their pre-season campaign with a five-star victory thanks to goals from Shea Lacey, Joshua Zirkzee, Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams

View 3 Images Manchester United thrashed Rosenborg in a friendly (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Wonderkid Shea Lacey grabbed his chance with both hands by scoring in Manchester United's first win of pre-season. The Red Devils lost 1-0 to Wrexham in Finland on Saturday and headed to Norway looking for a response against Rosenborg.

‌



Michael Carrick got the comfortable victory he was after, much thanks to Lacey's goal which broke the deadlock on 31 minutes. The striker, 19, raced away from Rosenborg's high line after being threaded through by Joshua Zirkzee, who started just one of Carrick's 17 games last term and has been heavily linked with a move to Juventus.

‌



As the Norwegian side scrambled back, Lacey showed his composure by cutting inside on his stronger left foot before curling a shot into the left-hand side of the net. It marked his first goal at senior level, albeit not in a competitive match, boosting the teenager's already high stock.

‌



The crowd, packed with United supporters, were delighted to see a goal - but Patrick Dorgu didn't seen too pleased with how it came about. The United star, playing on the left of midfield, wanted Lacey to square the ball across instead of going for goal himself. Dorgu throw his arms in the air, although he eventually came over to Lacey and congratulated him.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd drop clearest hint yet over Marcus Rashford's future as club bosses reach out READ MORE :

Enzo Maresca insists Man City won't repeat what Man Utd did after Sir Alex Ferguson READ MORE :

Leny Yoro hit the crossbar with a header before half-time, during which Carrick made a couple of changes. Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw made way for Jaydan Kamason and Harry Amass to make it a more youthful-looking XI.

‌



United kept up their dominance and doubled their lead shortly after the break, as Zirkzee went from provider to goalscorer in style. The Dutchman was initially involved in the build-up, spraying the ball out to Amass before getting it back on the edge of the penalty area.

Should Manchester United loan out Shea Lacey? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Shea Lacey opened his account in pre-season (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



After sending a defender for a hot dog with a cute body faint, Zirkzee pulled off the same trick again in front of the goalkeeper, allowing him to finish into an empty net. The 25-year-old only scored two goals last season - the most recent coming in December - and will be hoping for a more fruitful campaign this time around.

Carrick rung in the changes on the hour mark, making eight substitutions - all of them outfielders. The Fletcher twins, Tyler and Jack, were in midfield as Chido Obi led the line.

View 3 Images Joshua Zirkzee has been linked with Juventus (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



It took two minutes for midfielder Jacob Devaney to make an impact. When a corner kick fell kindly to him seven yards from goal, the Republic of Ireland youth international thrashed the ball into the roof of the net for 3-0.

Finally, Amass and Ethan Williams got in on the act, both finishing at the back post and giving Kamason two assists to cap an impressive second half. Next up for United, it's Atletico Madrid in Stockholm on Saturday, August 1.

Sports.title: World Cup match-fixing probe sparked after suspicious Spain match
Sports.content:
World Cup match-fixing probe sparked after suspicious Spain match

Spain's goalless draw with Cape Verde at the 2026 World Cup was such a stunning upset it was flagged as suspicious by the Council of Europe's betting monitoring unit

View 2 Images Spain's midfielder #16 Rodri (L) reacts after next to Cape Verde's goalkeeper #01 Vozinha (C) after missing a goal opportunity during the 2026 World Cup Group H football match between Spain and Cape Verde at the Atlanta Stadium in Atlanta on June 15, 2026. (Photo by Roberto SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images)

One of Spain’s matches on their way to winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup became the subject of a match-fixing probe.

‌



Spain won the tournament thanks to a 1-0 victory over Argentina in the final, having triumphed in all but one of their seven matches on their way to the climax at MetLife Stadium.

‌



The exception was a goalless draw with Cape Verde in their opening match of the World Cup, and the game was flagged as suspicious by the Council of Europe's betting monitoring unit, the Group of Copenhagen.

‌



Investigators were thought to be left surprised that Cape Verde managed to hold Spain to a goalless draw, and the match was played on ‘yellow notice’, meaning further investigation was required.

Premier League club forced to cancel pre-season friendly following G7 summit disruption READ MORE :

Argentina players ripped apart over World Cup chaos as FIFA set to take action READ MORE :

The draw was one of seven matches from the World Cup that the body has informed FIFA deserve to be looked into further.

Approximately £3.6m was staked with US cryptocurrency-based prediction market Polymarket on Spain failing to win what seemed at the tournament's outset to be a guaranteed victory.

‌



However, after officials examined betting patterns, intelligence and social media activity surrounding the outcome they concluded it was merely an extraordinary upset, as per the Daily Star.

They discovered Spain had 27 attempts compared to six for their rivals - but not one of the seven they directed on target could beat inspired Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha in the opening Group H encounter in Atlanta.

The 40-year-old produced stunning saves to thwart Mikel Oyarzabal, Aymeric Laporte and Ferran Torres - who also struck the crossbar as Spain bombarded the Cape Verde goal. The underdogs went on to draw with Uruguay and Saudi Arabia as well, securing qualification as group runners-up.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

They ultimately fell 3-2 to reigning world champions Argentina - following extra-time. Meanwhile, Spain defeated Argentina in the final.

FIFA's Integrity Task Force determined there was ‘no suspicious betting activity or indications of match manipulation’ and the Group of Copenhagen concurred - reclassifying it as 'green' or 'normal'.

‌



A source close to world football's governing body told the Daily Star: “It was a remarkable result. The fact it flagged up as a potentially suspicious result shows just how well Cape Verde did. But it was simply a huge shock. Shocks do happen in football.

“Argentina lost 2-1 to Saudi Arabia in their opening game in Qatar in 2022 and still went on to win the World Cup that year.

“Cape Verde were unbeaten this time in any match in 90 minutes. Argentina needed extra time to beat them. It was the kind of fairytale performance that makes the World Cup so special.”

‌



View 2 Images Vozinha holding up a Cape Verde flag after their draw against Spain (Image: Getty Images)

The Group of Copenhagen was among several independent organisations - including the FBI - scrutinising the tournament's 104 matches for evidence of potential fixing.

A red card issued to South Africa's Themba Zwane in the 84th minute of his team's tournament-opening clash against Mexico was also initially flagged yellow and subsequently de-classified to 'normal'.

‌



A three-and-a-half-minute delay from the video assistant referee team to disallow a goal from Spain's Ferran Torres in its 4-0 win over Saudi Arabia was also highlighted.

A surge of bets on US striker Folarin Balogun's red card ban being overturned so he could feature against Belgium in the last 16 was also flagged up.

His ban was suspended – which meant he could play – after Donald Trump made a personal plea to FIFA president Gianni Infantino. Belgium performed a 'Trump shuffle' on the pitch after hammering the US team 4-1.

‌



The Group of Copenhagen noted no other wagers were available on red card bans being overturned at the tournament.

However, FIFA told the Daily Star it backed the conclusions of its Integrity Task Force which had discovered no evidence of match outcome manipulation at the competition.

A spokesman said: “FIFA stands by the conclusions of its Integrity Task Force which is the result of a collaborative effort by a large number of independent expert groups.

Article continues below

“Betting‑monitoring reports and other relevant data and information provided by Task Force members, as well as information received through available reporting mechanisms, was analysed and shared among Task Force members in line with operational procedures.

“As a result no suspicious betting activity or indications of match manipulation in connection with any fixture was identified.”

Sports.title: Premier League club forced to cancel pre-season friendly following G7 summit disruption
Sports.content:
Premier League club forced to cancel pre-season friendly following G7 summit disruption

Brighton were due to face French second-tier side Annecy on Saturday, but the pre-season friendly has been cancelled after the pitches that Fabian Hurzeler's squad planned to train on become damaged

View 2 Images Donald Trump was among the world leaders to attend the G7 summit (Image: Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Brighton have cancelled a pre-season friendly in France after their training camp was plunged into chaos - by the helicopters used at the recent G7 summit. The Seagulls had planned base themselves at a hotel in Evian-les-Bains from Thursday, July 23 to Saturday, August 1 and use a set of nearby pitches to train.

‌



But those same pitches were used as landing grounds when world leaders flew in for June's G7 summit in the French spa town. Those who touched down included United States President Donald Trump, former UK prime minister Sir Keir Starmer and Emmanuel Macron, the president of France.

‌



The Athletic report that Brighton staff arrived at the hotel on Wednesday to prepare for the camp, only to report back that the pitches are unusable. The camp has been now abandoned and Saturday's friendly against Ligue 2 side Annecy won't go ahead.

‌



Brighton have now arranged an alternative camp in Austria and their game against French top-flight side Strasbourg is still expected to be played next Saturday. Fabian Hurzeler's squad have remained in the UK and will play an in-house match behind closed doors on Saturday before flying to Austria on Sunday.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



After returning from Austria, Brighton are due to host Italian opposition in the form of Roma and Bologna before the start of the new Premier League season. The 2026-27 campaign is set to be a hectic one, with the Seagulls have qualified for the Conference League play-offs.

The draw will take place on Monday, August 3. Brighton will start their Premier League season at home to Aston Villa before heading to Chelsea the following weekend.

Hurzeler has already brought in six new players this summer, including Tottenham centre-back Luka Vuskovic for a club-record £46million. It comes after Brighton sold Jan Paul van Hecke to Tottenham for £52m.

‌



Where will Brighton finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Brighton's preparations for the new season have been disrupted (Image: Lee Parker - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Brighton finished eighth last season and 'challenged the establishment', according to Hurzeler. "I think overall we did," the German said in a post-season interview with club media.

Article continues below

“Of course, we still see some improvements; we still see potential where we could have done better through the season, but overall we faced a lot of adversity, we faced a lot of challenges... But we always went through it; we always came back stronger."

Sports.title: Arsenal have been left without a choice as Mikel Arteta's transfer frustrations clear
Sports.content:
With over a month to go in the summer transfer window, the number of seismic deals that have already occurred would indicate that Premier League clubs are well on track to eclipse last year's record spend of £3billion.

While the majority of said deals have involved the league's elite, Arsenal have so far only added Christos Tzolis for £34million from Club Brugge with Illan Meslier, the former Leeds goalkeeper, also joining on a free transfer.

Strengthening a title-winning side is no mean feat and Arsenal have tried to be active. But the problem the Gunners have found is that they are trying to act rationally in a market which is now completely bereft of sanity.

Transfer fees have soared in recent years and are now well into obscene territory. And if the majority are moving with the tide rather than pushing against it, then that leaves others in a difficult spot.

‌



It has been well documented that Morgan Rogers was Arsenal's first choice target in their search for a new left attacker. They were widely regarded as the red-hot favourites to land him, but a gulf in valuations of the player between the champions and Aston Villa allowed Chelsea to swoop in. They were willing to make Rogers the most expensive British footballer of all time with a £117m package. Arsenal, though prepared to pay a premium on top of the £80m figure they valued Rogers at, were not.

There are similarities in their pursuit of Bruno Guimaraes: the Brazilian is an established quality operator at Premier League level and Newcastle have little to no appetite when it comes to a transfer. It's hard to see the situation unravelling to the extent that saw Alexander Isak complete his protracted move to Liverpool last year. An offer of £70m has been mooted for a player who, although top-class, turns 29 later this year. It's expected Newcastle will reject that out of hand — do Arsenal go much higher, if at all?

And therein lies the catch: although they may not want to, it could prove to be that they are left with little choice but to exceed their valuations for their top transfer targets if they are to attain the calibre of player they require to progress again after their title win.

The blockbuster transfer fees it has taken to acquire Rogers and Elliot Anderson (£116m) have already become benchmarks rather than a breaking point.

‌



If Arsenal are looking to level up then it's hard to see how they land a ceiling-raiser for the left wing berth without breaking the £100m barrier. Indeed, two other players they have been credited with an interest in, Bradley Barcola and Yan Diomande, are unlikely to move for less than a figure in that ballpark. Another mooted target, Julian Alvarez, would command an even greater fee in order for Atletico Madrid to consider selling.

The ripple effects of other deals have already been felt domestically in the market, too.

View 3 Images Arsenal could be priced out of a move for Bruno Guimaraes after already deciding against what would have been a club-record deal for Morgan Rogers (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Mateus Fernandes was pursued aggressively by Manchester United, but they were not willing to match the astronomic £85m package that Tottenham put down to sign him. It will not be lost on Arsenal or their supporters that their arch-rivals have not shied away from the vastly inflated fees now dominating the market, with Spurs also shelling out a mammoth £100m package to acquire Sandro Tonali. Both players were on Arsenal's radar earlier in the summer and it is not beyond the realms of possibility that other targets currently valued at more feasible figures suddenly skyrocket out of reach due to other deals.

‌



Arsenal ended an arduous 22-year title drought with their Premier League triumph last season. The hope is that such a wait does not occur again. But competition for their domestic crown will be fierce; Manchester City will come again, albeit without Pep Guardiola. Liverpool have a new manager and will expect to challenge for the title again. Chelsea, fresh off hijacking Arsenal's deal for Rogers, feel like they could also be back with Xabi Alonso at the helm.

Abstaining from paying the sort of monstrous transfer fees it seemingly now takes to acquire elite players could prove catastrophic if they harbour genuine ambitions of replicating the success of last season. Arteta has already made it crystal clear where he stands on that front.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola, another player Arsenal like, would likely command a transfer fee in excess of £100million (Image: Getty)

“We want to reach another level,” he said in the aftermath of Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain. “It is going to demand us to be very, very ambitious, very fast and very smart.”

‌



All of the teams listed above who will harbour title aspirations have broken the £100m barrier more than once since City made Jack Grealish the Premier League's first £100m player. Arsenal solitary foray into the nine-figure realm came back in 2023 to make Declan Rice their club-record signing.

With the current direction of the transfer market, Arsenal may have no choice but to do so again if they are to sign the players capable of matching Arteta's ambitions. Because transfer fees only seem to be going one way.

Sports.title: Hamilton fastest as Ferrari dominate Hungarian GP practice
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton edged his team-mate Charles Leclerc to the fastest time in second practice as Ferrari dominated the first day of running at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

After Leclerc had comfortably topped Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Hamilton in Friday's opening session, the seven-time world champion found major improvement later in the day to turn a half-second deficit into a 0.158s advantage over his team-mate.

The nearest challenger to Ferrari in the more representative second session was reigning world champion Lando Norris, who was just short of half a second back from Hamilton in his upgraded McLaren.

Hamilton said: "It was a solid day overall. The conditions were quite challenging, with the wind making things a bit tricky and the track feeling quite bumpy in some places.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Franco Colapinto lost control of his Alpine at the final corner before shunting into the barriers, causing a red flag in the middle of second practice

"The car felt better in FP2 and we made some good progress between the sessions, although there are still a few areas we need to improve. We'll go through all the data overnight, keep working on the balance and hopefully find a bit more performance for tomorrow."

While Ferrari's pace at the Hungaroring - a circuit many had assumed would suit their car - came as little surprise, the Italian team will be further buoyed by the unexpected struggles of championship leader Kimi Antonelli and his Mercedes team.

Having sat out the first session as Mercedes fulfilled one of their obligated rookie driver sessions, Antonelli struggled badly on his return to action as he repeatedly ran off track amid rear locking issues.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell admits Mercedes have work to do after a difficult practice in Hungary, with Ferrari looking strong and windy conditions adding to their challenges

The 19-year-old Italian, who leads Hamilton by 45 points at the top of the standings, was only 13th and almost two seconds off the pace, while his team-mate George Russell was almost a full second back from the lead time in fifth despite completing a flying lap on fresh soft tyres.

Verstappen was almost seven tenths off the pace in fourth, with his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar behind Russell in sixth.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who also sat out the first session, was a disappointing eighth as he was outpaced by Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson, but his deficit to team-mate Norris could potentially be explained by the Australian not having the same full upgrade package on his car.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aston Martin driver Lance Stroll avoids the barrier after failure leaves him stranded on track, triggering a red flag in P1 at the Hungarian Grand Prix

While Mercedes, along with McLaren and Red Bull, have time to make gains on Ferrari ahead of final practice at 11.30am on Saturday, the Italian team have established themselves as clear favourites for one of the season's most crucial qualifying sessions, which follows at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1.

The session was interrupted by a red flag for almost 10 minutes when Franco Colapinto heavily crashed his Alpine on entry to the final corner.

Aston Martin's Lance Stroll didn't feature after his suspension broke in first practice, with the team's woeful season continuing as their unveiling of a 16-part upgrade package was overshadowed by the incident.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso says Aston Martin’s new upgrades have delivered the improvements they expected, making the car easier to drive, but admits there is still more potential to unlock.

Fernando Alonso was at least able to exhibit some signs of improvement in their one working car in second practice, despite finishing between the two cars of 2026 newcomers Cadillac in 19th, almost three seconds off the pace.

Alonso had a significantly quicker lap deleted for a track limits breach, and the Spaniard said after the session that the car felt "much better" and had lived up to the team's expectations.

Sports.title: Fury not convinced Joshua will 'have the guts' to fight him
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury remains unconvinced that Anthony Joshua will agree to a long-awaited blockbuster British showdown, questioning whether his rival has the "guts" to face him.

Fury, speaking after his seventh-round stoppage of Mariusz Wach in a non-televised bout in Thailand on Friday, referenced Joshua opting not to get in the ring with him after his victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April.

Joshua's own tune-up fight ahead of a potential clash with Fury later this year comes in Saudi Arabia on Saturday as he takes on Kristian Prenga in what will be his first outing since he was a passenger in a car crash in Nigeria in December that killed two of his close friends.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking before Fury vs Wach, Anthony Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn hit back at Fury's claims he was worried about a potential bout against AJ falling through

Fury said of AJ: "I got through my test. Let's see if [Joshua] gets through his test. The biggest test of it all is how big his balls are. I think he's a big s***house.

"In Tottenham in front of 70,000 people, he never had the guts to get in the ring and face me. Let's see if he ever does. I'm not convinced.

"I'll regroup. Hopefully the next big fight is signed next week, and we head wherever we're going to head.

"Is it gonna be in Vegas? Is it gonna be in New York? Is it gonna be in Ireland? Is it gonna be in London? Who knows, Belfast maybe? It might even be here in Pattaya, Thailand!"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joshua responded to Fury's claim about not being interested in watching his fight, casting doubt over a potential bout between the two later this year.

Fury: I'm definitely not attending AJ fight in Jeddah

Fury - whose clash with Joshua could take place at Wembley at 2am in order to work for a global audience - maintains he will not head to Jeddah to face-off with AJ this weekend.

The 37-year-old said: "I've been away the last six or seven months. I'm definitely not going to Jeddah. I'm going home to my wife and kids who have been supporting me from a distance.

"I've been away in training camp for 10 weeks. I was away before that for four months, so I'm going to go home and have a rest."

Image: Fury's record is now 36-2-1, with his 40th career bout now potentially against Joshua

Fury was also insistent that he needed to fight Polish veteran Wach three months on from a points win over Russia's Makhmudov, adding: "I've had one fight in two years.

"This is my second fight in two years. Of course, I wanted to get the rounds in. I want to be active.

"It's not just the boxing in the ring. It's the fight week - the press conference, the weigh-in, the nerves, everything."

Sports.title: AJ weighs in at 251lbs for Prenga bout
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua weighed in 7.6lbs heavier than his last fight against Jake Paul, as the British boxer prepares to face Kristian Prenga on Saturday night in Jeddah.

Joshua took to the scales on Friday at 251lbs, having weighed 243.4lbs when he beat YouTube boxer Paul in December 2025.

Albanian Prenga scaled 261.4lbs, 10.4lbs heavier than Joshua.

The heaviest Joshua has ever been for a fight is 255.4lbs when he defeated Jermaine Franklin in April 2023.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joshua faces a tough fight against the Albanian, who has lost just one of his 21 fights

"We're feeling good. It's going down tomorrow night in Jeddah," Joshua said to DAZN Boxing.

The weigh-in came after Tyson Fury claimed a seventh-round TKO victory over Mariusz Wach in Thailand.

Fury said that he had 'got through' his test but was doubtful that Joshua would overcome tomorrow night's opponent, Prenga.

The 35-year-old Albanian will be a formidable opponent for Joshua, with Prenga having lost only once in his 21-fight career, having claimed each of his last 16 victories via knock-out or TKO.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On Friday, Tyson Fury claimed victory over Mariusz Wach in Thailand and said he would not be coming to watch Joshua's fight

"The work is done and this isn't going to be easy," Eddie Hearn told DAZN Boxing.

"[Prenga] isn't a guy coming in here with a bundle of defeats, coming for a payday. He's got the whole of Albania behind him by the sounds of things as well.

"Big fight, big opportunity. We know what comes the other side; we've just got to deal with this guy tonight.

"I expect, and I hope, that we get a performance that shows everything that Joshua has put into this training camp."

Usyk's team demanding 'greatness' from Joshua

Joshua, who hasn't fought since he stepped into the ring to face Paul in December 2025, has been training with Oleksandr Usyk's team to prepare for tomorrow's fight.

He revealed in the build-up to tomorrow's fight that Usyk's team have encouraged him to 'show greatness' against Prenga this weekend.

"I'm quite good at what I do anyway," Joshua told Sky Sports. "I'm quite strong. I can take, I can give, so sometimes I can just get away with doing enough but still be good enough.

"But these guys are like, 'nah'. They want to see more. They want to see more, like bring it out.

"Let's bring out the good stuff that you've got in you and let's improve. And my approach to training has definitely improved a lot."

He added: "You're performing at your best, but it should be normal to perform at this level. That's what Usyk's team were saying. Your greatness should just be something that you do every day in the gym."

Sports.title: Mercedes fears over Ferrari pace realised - Russell
Sports.content:
George Russell admitted Mercedes' fears about Ferrari's likely strong pace at the Hungarian Grand Prix materialised in a Friday practice dominated by their world championship rivals.

Mercedes lead the world championship battles with eight wins from 10 races so far but the tight and twisty nature of Hungaroring had led to suggestions in the build-up to this event that Ferrari, the winners of the season's other two grands prix and whose car's strengths lie in cornering, could be the ones to beat this weekend.

Those expectations at least proved accurate on Friday with the Italian team comfortably topping both practice sessions, including a one-two for Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in the more-representative second hour of running.

Mercedes, by contrast, finished second practice only fifth and 13th fastest - with an unusually-large 0.9s gap to their chief rivals amid balance struggles on single-lap pace. Lando Norris was third in a heavily-upgraded McLaren and Red Bull's Max Verstappen fourth.

"It was quite a strange day out there I think for everybody," said fifth-fastest Russell.

"Budapest is an amazing track to drive but they've resurfaced half the track, super bumpy, a lot of it is breaking up around the last couple of corners which is making it quite strange to drive on.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell admits Mercedes have work to do after a difficult practice in Hungary, with Ferrari looking strong and windy conditions adding to their challenges

"Our single lap [pace] didn't look great. The long run looked more competitive but what what we, I guess, potentially feared with Ferrari seemed to be the case.

"They look very, very strong."

Championship leader Antonelli, who sat out first practice while the team fulfilled rookie-driver running requirements with Frederic Vesti, was down in 13th with his soft-tyre runs compromised by an untimely red flag for Franco Colapinto's crash and then his own driving errors, including a big lock-up at Turn Two.

Russell added: "We've got work to do as a team. Ferrari are a good step ahead of everyone right now.

"I think for both Kimi and I the car was far from great, to be honest, and we think there is room to improve.

"It was really windy today and I think the wind [direction] is going to be shifting so that could be changing a lot."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Franco Colapinto lost control of his Alpine at the final corner before shunting into the barriers, causing a red flag in the middle of second practice

Ferrari pleased with fast start but wary of large early advantage

Although they have benefited from some good fortune, Ferrari's two race wins so far this year have come in the last four races. Hungary marked just the second time all season that they had finished a conventional Friday fastest of all.

Leclerc topped the opening session by a massive 0.4s margin before slotting in 0.148s behind Hamilton in second practice, and said: "It was a relatively strong day.

"From the beginning I felt quite good with the car and performance seemed to be good straight away. So that's a good thing but the weekend is still long and from the Friday to the Saturday we see teams making a jump of performance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Look back at some of the most dramatic moments throughout the years at the Hungarian Grand Prix

"Normally we are on the back foot on the Friday so it's a good thing we have a good Friday, but we still need to stay on it and work hard in order to get better.

"It's going to be tight [in qualifying] as always. I don't expect us to be having the gap that we had today, so we'll have to do everything perfect. But if the feeling is there I'm sure we'll do a good job in Q3."

Hamilton added in Ferrari's end-of-day press release: "It was a solid day overall. The conditions were quite challenging, with the wind making things a bit tricky and the track feeling quite bumpy in some places.

"The car felt better in FP2 and we made some good progress between the sessions, although there are still a few areas we need to improve. We'll go through all the data overnight, keep working on the balance and hopefully find a bit more performance."

Image: Hungary was the scene of Lewis Hamilton's last Grand Prix pole position in 2023

In keeping with his drivers, team principal Frederic Vasseur was also not getting carried away by Friday's lofty placing.

"So far, so good, but it's not on Friday we are doing the pole, even less that you win the race," he stressed.

"It's good to start the weekend like this but let's see tomorrow, it will be another story. I think [third-fastest] Norris didn't finish the lap… we will see tomorrow."

Ferrari's speed nonetheless caught the eye elsewhere too.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, who finished sixth quickest, said: "I knew they were going to be quick on a track like that. At the moment we are waiting for Mercedes to wake up.

"Like always I think it's going to be very close with the McLarens. That's where we are at the moment."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Look back at some of the most dramatic moments throughout the years at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Oscar Piastri, eighth quickest in the one McLaren that didn't carry their significant upgrade on Friday, added: "The Ferraris have looked very quick in both sessions.

"But I think Lando looked competitive in that [second] one especially.

"The Mercedes is very hard to read. So let's see tomorrow. If we execute a good day then it looks like there could be a lot up for grabs."

Sports.title: Liverpool takeover Q&A: Could Bezos buy stake at Anfield?
Sports.content:
Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group are in talks with a consortium fronted by Amit Bhatia over the sale of a minority stake in the club.

It has since emerged that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos - the world's third richest person - has been approached to join the syndicate of investors.

We take a look at some of the key questions surrounding what could be one of the most extraordinary deals involving a Premier League club in recent times...

Who are Bhatia and Bezos?

Bhatia is a 46-year-old British Indian entrepreneur, who has an investment banking background.

Image: Amit Bhatia is the former co-owner of Queen's Park Rangers

He currently manages a multi-asset investment firm called AyBe Capital which invests in range of diversified sectors including technology, media, property and real estate, consumer retail, and health.

Bhatia is married to Vanisha Mittal Bhatia, who is the daughter of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

Bezos is one of the most famous businessmen in the world and the owner of e-commerce giant Amazon, which he founded in 1994 out of his Seattle garage.

His other investments include aerospace company Blue Origin and venture capital firm Nash Holdings, which is the ownership vehicle for The Washington Post.

What are they worth?

It's unclear how much Bhatia himself is worth. But his father-in-law, billionaire steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, is worth an estimated £23.2bn according to Forbes. That makes him the 72nd richest person in the world.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky News' Mark Kleinman discusses Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' potential involvement in a consortium - led by former QPR co-owner Amit Bhatia - that is trying to buy a stake in Liverpool

Bezos is far wealthier than Mittal. Forbes estimates that his personal fortune is in the region of $245bn (£184bn), making him the third-richest person in the world behind Elon Musk and Google co-founder Larry Page.

What are their sporting interests?

Bhatia was just 28 when he joined the board of directors and became vice-chairman of QPR in 2007 after the Mittal family bought a 20 per cent stake in QPR, joining Bernie Ecclestone and Flavio Briatore as investors in the London club.

He spent five years as QPR chairman between 2018 and 2023 and stayed on as a director and co-owner until earlier this week when he transferred his stake in the club to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amit Bhatia is leading a consortium in an attempt to purchase a minority stake in Liverpool - we take a closer look at the former QPR co-owner

Through AyBe capital, Bhatia is an investor in TGL - Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods' golf league which fuses golf and technology and features six teams with some of the best players in the world in a season-long competition.

His firm also invests in Switch Hitter, which is a media brand founded by Kevin Pietersen, delivering exclusive interviews and content with the world's top cricketers.

Image: Rajasthan Royals were one of the most sought-after IPL cricket franchises

Earlier this year, Bhatia's father-in-law acquired a 75 per cent stake in the Rajasthan Royals Indian Premier League cricket franchise.

Bezos is a big American Football fan and has previously been reported to have explored bids for both the Washington Commanders and the Seattle Seahawks.

Image: Amazon co-founder Jeff Bezos is known to be a big American Football fan

He is not known to hold a significant stake in any sports team or enterprise currently. Interestingly, he did attend the Round of 16 World Cup clash between USA and Belgium in Seattle earlier this month and was accompanied by his wife Lauren Sanchez Bezos.

Why would FSG want to sell?

FSG are under no pressure to sell but did indicate in 2022 that they were open to new investment in Liverpool, with the sale of a small stake to Dynasty Equity completed the following year.

Liverpool have enjoyed huge success under FSG, lifting every major trophy available to win.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Football finance expert Kieran Maguire explains what a 'strategic minority stake' is and if a potential deal could signal the end of Fenway Sports Group as Liverpool owners

FSG may think it's mission accomplished somewhat as far they're concerned and are therefore amenable to fresh investment. They also stand to make a huge profit on their initial investment - even if they sell a percentage stake in the club.

How much do Bhatia and Bezos want to buy and what could the deal be worth?

There is no confirmation of the stake in Liverpool that the consortium wants to buy, but reports indicate that it could be anything up to 30 per cent. What the deal would be worth depends entirely on the stake Bhatia and co are interesting in acquiring.

What is the club valued at?

Liverpool are the fourth most valuable club in the world. They have most recently been valued at £4.7bn by Forbes, behind Manchester United (£5.4bn), Barcelona (£5.6bn) and Real Madrid who are worth a whopping £7.1bn.

Who owns Liverpool?

FSG have complete control of Liverpool, but private equity firms RedBird Capital and Arctos Sports Partners both hold minority stakes in the club. Dynasty Equity are also passive investors in Liverpool after injecting £164m into the club in 2023.

Image: The Anfield home of Liverpool Football Club

How much did FSG pay for Liverpool?

FSG were known as New England Sports Ventures when they paid £300m for Liverpool in October 2010 after a tumultuous period under former owners Tom Hicks and George Gillette.

When could the deal go ahead?

There is no timeframe as it stands, but the deal is still at a relatively early stage and it is expected that any potential transaction could take months rather than weeks to complete.

Who else is involved?

Bhatia has been confirmed as the person heading up the consortium. Sky News exclusively revealed that Bezos had been approached by Bhatia to join the investment group but the identity of any other potential investors is unknown at this stage.

Sports.title: Alonso pleased with Aston Martin upgrade as Newey targets 'respectability'
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso said the performance of his Aston Martin was "much better" as the team debuted a huge upgrade package during Hungarian Grand Prix practice on Friday.

Aston Martin had approached F1's latest generation of rules, which kicked in at the start of this season, as a major opportunity to break into the sport's established 'big four' teams and challenge for titles.

Instead, they have endured a woeful campaign, with a massively underperforming Honda engine and a chassis, the design of which was led by team boss Adrian Newey, failing to meet expected standards.

While other teams have brought several upgrade packages throughout the year, Aston Martin have waited until the 11th round in Budapest to bring one mega-package of 16 new parts.

It was a mixed day for the team as the left-rear suspension on Lance Stroll's car failed during first practice and ruled him out of the second session, but Alonso was left reasonably satisfied after managing a relatively normal day of running.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso says Aston Martin’s new upgrades have delivered the improvements they expected, making the car easier to drive, but admits there is still more potential to unlock

"It was much better," Alonso said. "The car felt more glued to the ground and easier to drive, to an extent, when you are in control of the grip in the corners.

"A more predictable and easier car, but still a long way to go for us. Obviously, this is only the first step."

The chassis upgrade comes a round ahead of Honda's expected delivery of a major engine upgrade at the Dutch Grand Prix after the summer break.

Alonso continued: "We need to find more performance both on the chassis not but also on the engine. Zandvoort will be a good test for us with the new engine. Step by step, but definitely in the direction.

"It looks better, for sure, and it's more or less what we expected. This is the most encouraging thing, that what we thought the new package would do the car actually translated into reality on track.

"That kind of correlation is what we need also for next year's project, so I think there is a positive atmosphere in the team now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aston Martin driver Lance Stroll avoids barrier after failure leaves him stranded on track, triggering red flag in P1 at the Hungarian Grand Prix

While Alonso's position of 19th on the timesheet in second practice appeared underwhelming as he finished between the two cars of 2026 newcomers Cadillac, he lost a significantly faster lap due to a breach of track limits.

That, along with traffic and an unhelpful red-flag interruption caused by Alpine's Franco Colapinto crashing out of the session, gave Alonso hope he can find more pace on Saturday.

"I think it was tricky with the red flag and some of the traffic to maximise the lap," Alonso said.

"So, maybe there is a little bit more to come from our side, but maybe it's the same for everybody, so let's see tomorrow.

"[We] concentrated on testing the new parts and trying to understand the setup direction, which maybe can be very different to what we've run at the last few events, so I think there is more potential to unlock hopefully tonight and into tomorrow's qualy."

Newey: Immediate goal is respectability

Newey, who arrived at Aston Martin from Red Bull in March 2025 as the most decorated designer in the sport's history, admitted his short-term target is the team achieving "respectability".

Speaking in a press conference between Friday's two sessions, Newey said: "The first races have been a complete nightmare.

"Hopefully, we can get at least a point and respectability now. I think that is the immediate goal. From there, we can try to keep moving forward."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aston Martin team principal Adrian Newey is optimistic their recent upgrades will boost the performance of the cars

Newey was speaking before Stroll had been ruled out of second practice, as a result of the team being unable to repair the Canadian's car in time for the session.

He did well to avoid the barriers when the left-rear of his car suddenly broke and caused him to spin in the latter stages of the opening session.

Newey admitted that the team were initially unsure of what had caused the problem.

He said at the time: "As you can imagine, everybody is feverishly trying to understand exactly what went wrong and what happened as we speak.

"It's only once we have an understanding that we can comment on what we do next."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Newey revealed that the part the part that broke on Stroll's car was not actually a new one, but the issue was complicated by the fact it was surrounded by new parts.

"The area involved was actually not changed," Newey added.

"We are short on spares because the cladding and so forth is different, so there are some minor changes in that area. In that sense, it's very unexpected."
