Sports.title: ‘You need to evolve’: Enzo Maresca plots life after Pep at Manchester City
Sports.content:
Relaxed and tanned, Enzo Maresca offered a warm note with his first words to the media as the manager of Manchester City, who must somehow follow the generational Pep Guardiola. “Before we start, I would like to send a message and a big hug to Kevin Keegan’s family for this moment,” said the Italian in tribute to a football legend, following his death on Monday.

Keegan, of course, was a former City manager who had at Newcastle famously locked horns with Sir Alex Ferguson when he led Manchester United, the fierce rivals of Maresca’s new team. When the 46-year-old, sat on the dais occupied for 10 mostly glittering years by Guardiola, offered an unsolicited reference to Ferguson – and Arsène Wenger – you could see he comprehended the mammoth task before him.

How do you follow the man who claimed 20 trophies in a decade and who ranks alongside Ferguson? Well, by mentioning, and so trying to tame, the elephant in the room. “The history of the manager with many years in the same club always struggled a little bit. After Sir Alex, after Arsène,” Maresca said. “But also, it’s a challenge to try to do the right things immediately for this organisation, for the fans, for everyone.”

Speaking in front of a giant “Welcome back Enzo” billboard, a reference to his previous leading of City’s elite development squad in 2020-21 as well as his stint as Guardiola’s assistant manager in the 2022-23 treble season, Maresca would have been aware the font of goodwill will not prove deep if results go south. Certainly not from that most fickle of constituencies – fans. So Maresca cutely pointed to the patience of City’s chairman, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, and his executive. “This club has had three managers in 17 years,” he said. “This is not normal, so this is one of the things that I’m confident we can do a great job and continue to do the job that has been done in the last years. Roberto [Mancini] was here, then Manuel [Pellegrini] and then Pep – for 10 years.”

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca with Pep Guardiola at a June 2023 Manchester City training session. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

Mancini’s tenure began in December 2009, ended with his sacking in May 2013, and was angst-ridden: anathema to al-Mubarak and his chief executive, Ferran Soriano. If Mancini could be volatile, Pellegrini proved serene, and Guardiola was, simply, a genius. Al-Mubarak’s and Soriano’s experience of Maresca during his two previous seasons at City obviously convinced them that he is the full package: an accomplished football man who is of equable character.

Yet Maresca’s exit from his previous post at Chelsea on New Year’s Day ended with an apology from him, and City paying the west London club £17m in compensation. Maresca’s shutters came down for the first – and only – time when his conduct was raised. “I feel quite lucky in terms of my former clubs – Leicester, Chelsea – I think we did a great job,” he said. “In both clubs, the identity of the team was clear, the success of the team was clear, and I feel very lucky to be part of these clubs. But now we are here today. That is the most important thing, just about City. And nothing to add.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Maresca made Leicester Championship champions and the next season took Chelsea to fourth in the Premier League and a Conference League triumph before claiming the Fifa Club World Cup last summer, a 3-0 evisceration of Paris Saint-Germain in the final a calling card that may well have sealed the City job.

He talked of “titles” for the coming season. To aid this mission, Maresca has Elliot Anderson, a £116m buy from Nottingham Forest, to patrol midfield, and potentially Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, who shone for Morocco at the World Cup, to further bolster this department. He also retains an interest in Malo Gusto, one of his right-backs when at Chelsea, and if Omar Marmoush leaves, the market will be entered for a similar, pacy forward.

One player Maresca certainly does not wish to lose is the peerless Rodri, who lifted the World Cup for Spain on Sunday and received the Golden Ball, and whose control of a contest in the ever-more frantic domestic game is priceless. The 30-year-old will have surgery on a back problem on Monday. The word is it is not too serious, though he will miss out when City host Bournemouth on the opening weekend of the season. The more important date is 1 September, when the transfer window closes: will Real Madrid have made a move for a footballer who has a year left on his terms and is declining to sign the new deal offered by City?

Of more immediate concern for Maresca is flying out on Tuesday for a pre‑season tour of Asia that features matches with Inter in Hong Kong and K-League All Stars and Atlético Madrid in Seoul. For the trip Maresca will have back City’s A-listers who exited the World Cup early, including Josko Gvardiol, Mateo Kovacic and Abdukodir Khusanov.

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson was a key player for England at the World Cup and was Manchester City’s first signing of the summer. Photograph: Marta Lavandier/AP

“I’m working at the moment with many young players,” he said. “That is always good because they are full of energy and some of them are very good. The last group of players are going to join three or four days before the Community Shield and we will have all the squad.” After that Cardiff game with Arsenal on Sunday 16 August, the bid to successfully succeed Guardiola begins in earnest.

“You need to adapt, evolve,” Maresca added in reference to his playing style. “Set pieces, man to man – it’s a little bit the direction where football is going. We managers, it’s our duty to find solutions.” We are about to discover how good he is at this.

Sports.title: Jürgen Klopp vows to change Germany but threatens to quit if family hounded by media
Sports.content:
Jürgen Klopp said he wants his team to “change a country” after being confirmed as Germany’s new head coach, but threatened to stand down if his family are hounded by the media during his time in charge.

In a forthright first press conference upon his unveiling as Julian Nagelsmann’s replacement, Klopp also suggested the role will be his final job in top-level football and expressed regret after poking fun at his predecessor while working as a television pundit during the World Cup. He is tasked with reviving Germany, who lost to Paraguay in the last 32 and have not made the last 16 since winning the tournament in 2014.

It marks a return to the dugout for Klopp two years after leaving Liverpool, where he ended a glorious nine-season tenure after explaining he felt fatigued. Since January 2025 he has worked as head of global soccer for Red Bull but a comeback to frontline action had appeared inevitable since Nagelsmann departed on 3 July.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp was in forthright mood in his first press conference as Germany head coach. Photograph: Hannes Albert/EPA

Klopp vowed to transform a deeply fractured relationship between the national team and Germany’s public, citing his work at Liverpool as an example of the way football can galvanise a wider community.

“I want to create a situation where fans go home after the game and say: ‘Wow, that was cool,’” he said. “I want people to say: ‘Wow, it was worth putting the TV on for 90 minutes to see Germany play.’ I’ve lived and experienced how football can change a city. And I think it’s not only about cities, it’s also about the country. Ideally, football can change a country.”

The 59-year-old’s contract will run until after the 2030 World Cup. Klopp, however, warned that he would not tolerate invasive treatment from journalists and that he would be prepared to depart without compensation if he felt his family’s privacy had been violated.

“I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you treated Nagelsmann,” he said. “I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you’ve treated, in England, Thomas Tuchel. The day you don’t want me any more, I’m gone, without any severance pay. If you say tomorrow: ‘He’s shit,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away.

“Criticise me if something doesn’t work. Jürgen Klopp is not going to have any career after the national team. This is the pinnacle of my career as a coach. I will give it everything I’ve got.”

Klopp was criticised last month when, speaking with the former Germany player Thomas Müller on television during coverage of the group stage match with Curaçao, he appeared to hint Nagelsmann’s days were numbered by saying he was “still” picking the team. That was followed by a quick apology; Klopp repeated the sentiment on Friday and said the pair have yet to speak since his appointment was confirmed.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp, in his role as Magenta TV pundit, with Kylian Mbappé after France’s World Cup quarter-final against Morocco. Photograph: Greg M Cooper/EPA

“We haven’t had any exchange,” he said, wishing Nagelsmann a happy 39th birthday for Thursday. “It was a joke. In retrospect it was one of the worst ‘funny’ remarks I have ever made. I feel awfully sorry, I’ve apologised a million times.

“It was just a rash thing to say, with no ulterior motive whatsoever, and I can only wish him the best.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Now he can go on to pastures new and I’m absolutely sure he will have many opportunities to coach a big team in future.”

Klopp promised Germany will play expansive football with wingers but admitted they must find their own way to compete with the depth of talent available elsewhere. “Success is performance relative to expectations,” he said. “When we ask in Germany: ‘Are we as good as France?’ and the answer is no, that’s not true. If we ask: ‘Do we have players like Dembélé, Mbappé, Doué and Barcola?’, no we don’t, but we can still beat them.

“We don’t want to play like Argentina, Spain, England or France. We want to do it the German way, very intense. Are we the No 1 team right now? No, we accept that. There are 11 teams ahead of us in the ranking. We can beat them, but for this to happen we need to play very good, very intense football.”

International football will demand a change of rhythm for Klopp after a lifetime spent in the domestic game. “I think contact with a team is not necessarily about working with them day in, day out,” he said. “Sometimes it will be 30 minutes or an hour and that will be on the pitch. But all of them have a mobile. I’ll talk to them, listen to them, watch games and give my feedback. That, too, is developing players and making them better.”

Klopp’s reign will begin with a ­baptism of fire in Amsterdam against the Netherlands on 24 September, one of four Nations League games in the space of 11 days. “The players have to show me, and not just say it, that playing for Germany is a super special thing,” he said.

Sports.title: Dismissed solicitor is still acting for footballers in brain injury court case
Sports.content:
The solicitor dismissed by a group of over 1,000 rugby players with brain injuries who are suing the sport’s governing bodies is still leading a similar claim on behalf of dozens of former footballers.

Richard Boardman told a hearing at the Royal Courts of Justice this week of his intention to “come off the record,” with the claimants indicating that they had unanimously agreed to terminate their dealings with his firm, Rylands Garth.

Boardman’s management of the case was strongly criticised by the presiding judge, Master Jeremy Cook, who highlighted alleged “widespread non-compliance” and “misleading evidence,” with particular regard to his failure to make good on a pledge to provide the court with all of the claimants’ medical records.

Master Cook is now considering whether to strike off the case entirely, which would leave a large cohort of former union and league players including England World Cup winners Steve Thompson and Phil Vickery with nothing to show for six years of gruelling legal battles.

Despite being dismissed by the rugby players however, Boardman is still acting on behalf of a group of 23 former footballers who are suing the Football Association, English Football League and FA of Wales as a result of permanent brain injuries sustained during their careers.

The group includes the families of World Cup hero Nobby Stiles, former Newcastle manager Joe Kinnear and four former players from the Premier League era. With a far smaller number of claimants, and as a result fewer medical records, the football case is seen as more manageable for Rylands Garth.

Coincidentally, the FA changed their defence team in the case earlier this year and both parties remain in the process of exchanging documents.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The rugby claimants are in the process of appointing new solicitors, but until they have done so Boardman remains notionally in charge despite being absent from court for the last day and a half of hearings this week. The firm Leigh Day has been consulting on the case since February and is considering whether to take it on.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola backs backroom staff to help cure Liverpool’s set-piece ills
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has outlined the roles his backroom staff will play in trying to improve Liverpool’s set-piece record next season and admitted he was “very lucky” to inherit a talented coaching team at Bournemouth.

Iraola has brought several members of his Bournemouth backroom team with him to Liverpool since succeeding Arne Slot last month. Tommy Elphick, a boyhood Liverpool fan, and Shaun Cooper have joined as first-team coaches while Iraola’s long-time colleague Pablo de la Torre has arrived as assistant coach. Alejandro Rosalen has taken over as first-team goalkeeping coach after five years with Napoli.

Iraola worked alongside De la Torre in his first coaching job at AEK Larnaca, and again at Rayo Vallecano, and said having trusted confidants alongside him would be invaluable for his first season in charge at Anfield. “For me, it was important they came with me,” said Iraola, who will take charge of his first Liverpool game on Saturday in a pre-season friendly against Sunderland in Nashville. “Pablo is a physical coach but has been with me almost all the years I have been coaching. So, for me, he is much more than a physical coach really. He is an assistant and we know each other very well.

“I was very lucky with Tommy and Shaun when I arrived at Bournemouth. Because I was unlucky to have the issue with my assistant coach Iñigo Pérez [who was denied a work permit when attempting to follow Iraola from Rayo Vallecano to Bournemouth]. After, it worked out very well for him because now he is coaching Villarreal. Maybe we play him in the Champions League.

“But when I had Tommy and Shaun there, we did not feel the need to bring in another assistant. They were very prepared, they were very helpful for me in terms of understanding the English culture, the mentality of the players, what they were used to, what they like in training, even the small details that maybe in Spain are different. Also the experience Tommy has at Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Huddersfield; they can be in a closer position to the players. They can feel more identified. I am a little bit older. Some of the players maybe didn’t know I was a player.”

One requirement for Iraola and his backroom staff will be to address Liverpool’s problems at set pieces. Only Bournemouth (26), Crystal Palace (25) and Leeds (24) conceded more set-piece goals than Liverpool’s 23 in what proved Slot’s final season as head coach, having won the title in his first. “They are very good coaches,” said Iraola. “We kind of ­understand the game similarly and they have different roles in the coaching staff, they help with set pieces also. That’s the reason I continued with them.

“Tommy does defensive set plays, Shaun does more offensive, more ­creative ones. But also we are working very well here with the set-piece analyst [Lewis Mahoney], who was very good in the second half of last season. He is already with the club, so they are working on some stuff.”

Sports.title: Transfer news: Newcastle sign Monaco’s Bamba, Summerville joins Al-Hilal
Sports.content:
Newcastle have made Aladji Bamba their fourth signing of the summer after the 20-year-old midfielder ­completed a move from Monaco for a fee that could rise to £34m.

“I’m very happy to be here,” said Bamba. “I was very excited when I heard Newcastle were interested in signing me. I know about the ­history of the club and I’ve visited the ­stadium, which is amazing. I can’t wait to be on the pitch.”

Bamba, who has agreed a five-year contract, is Newcastle’s fourth signing this summer aged 20 or under. The France youth midfielder – who made 25 appearances for Monaco last season, impressing in Ligue 1 and the Champions League – joins the ­former Reims goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (20), the former Hoffenheim winger Bazoumana Touré (also 20) and the former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur (18). As a natural No 6, Bamba will be expected to compete with Lewis Miley for the midfield anchor role vacated when Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham for an initial £92.5m.

Newcastle’s transfer policy is to sign players aged 24 or under ­costing, broadly, between £20m and £40m and possessing high resale potential. The idea is to help ensure a club that have recently negotiated a three-year settlement agreement with Uefa after breaching European spending rules remain on the right side of football’s squad investment regulations.

“Aladji adds a range of ­qualities to our midfield with huge ­potential for growth,” said Eddie Howe, ­Newcastle’s head coach. “His ­development since breaking through at Monaco has been really ­impressive and is something we believe we can build on.”

Howe hopes Bruno ­Guimarães will be at Newcastle to ease Bamba’s ­adaptation to Premier League life. The Brazil midfielder is wanted by Arsenal and appears keen to join Mikel Arteta’s team. However, the price is a stumbling block. ­Newcastle’s ­reluctance to sell their captain dictates they have let it be known through intermediaries that they will reject any offer in the region of £70m for a player who turns 29 in November.

Arsenal have still to make a formal offer and whether they are prepared to go beyond £75m remains to be seen. Much may hinge on whether Guimarães returns to Newcastle from a holiday in Brazil, as planned, next week before joining his teammates at a training camp at La Manga in southern Spain.

Summerville seals £60m Al-Hilal move

Crysencio Summerville has left West Ham to join the Saudi Arabian club Al Hilal, the Hammers have announced.

The Netherlands winger joined West Ham from Leeds two years ago but was unable to prevent their relegation to the Championship last season. After previous links with Italian club Roma, the 24-year-old has signed a four-year contract with Al-Hilal.

“West Ham United would like to thank Crysencio for his service and wish him well for the future,” the Hammers said in a statement. The club are yet to make any new signings this summer, but their transfer budget will be boosted by Summerville’s fee – an initial £55m, rising to a possible £60m with add-ons.

View image in fullscreen Crysencio Summerville has left West Ham for Al-Hilal after two seasons at the club. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Hull City have signed the Japan midfielder Hidemasa Morita on a two-year deal, with a club option of a further year. The 31-year-old, who has won 40 caps for his country, joins as a free agent after leaving Portuguese club Sporting.

Everton have confirmed the departure of midfielder Idrissa Gana Gueye, who leaves after 236 appearances in two separate spells. Gueye’s contract expired on 30 June, and talks over a potential extension have come to nothing. He is expected to sign a one-year deal with Saudi club Al-Diriyah in due course.

“Everyone at Everton is hugely grateful for Gana’s dedication on the pitch throughout his two spells at the club,” said the club’s manager, David Moyes. His commitment to the club over many years was exceptional.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Manchester United and the quest to make mythical midfield a reality
Sports.content:
MIDDLE MEN

Like the urban myth that you are never more than three feet away from a spider, modern footballing lore tells us Manchester United are only ever three signings away from a Premier League title challenge. With the Geopolitics World Cup in the rear-view mirror and the transfer news machine churning once more, you may have missed United being linked with just about every midfielder to ever grace a centre circle. They missed out on Elliot Anderson – who went and dubbed his new club the “kings of Manchester” – and were fooled into thinking they could snare Aurélien Tchouaméni. They danced briefly with Atalanta’s Éderson, before landing on Chelsea resale project prospect Andrey Santos and former Aston Villa linchpin Youri Tielemans. And United aren’t done with their midfield overhaul – rightly so given they have lost Casemiro to Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte to long-term knee knack. Next up on United’s extensive longlist: Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga and Fulham’s Sander Berge, plus France GWC sensation Manu Koné as Michael Carrick eyes the final piece in his midfield puzzle.

The problem with United over the past 13 years has been that it’s never actually the final piece. It would be kind to call their post-Ferguson transfer hit rate scattergun. Ángel Di María was the first final piece in the puzzle. Then it was Alexis Sánchez. Then Fred. And then Jadon Sancho. Something needed to change. So say what you like about Big Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s recent, purse-tightening Old Trafford regime, but they’ve not flopped anywhere near as hard in the transfer market as their predecessors. Only Ugarte and Joshua Zirkzee can be deemed true flops under the Ineos boys. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha were smart additions a year ago, Senne Lammens was a scouting triumph and United are threatening to go again with their sensible signings policy – who’d have thunk it?! – with a combined £85m on Santos and Tielemans representing far better value than splashing that same amount on relegation specialist Matheus Fernandes. Finding value in the market is almost impossible nowadays, but credit to these fellas, they’re giving it a go.

What feels quite apt with Carrick at the wheel is that United’s biggest struggle this summer has been to find a true midfield destroyer. That moniker certainly doesn’t fit Santos, nor Tielemans. Tchouaméni was always unattainable so United are getting creative, as they did when Carrick was sought as Roy Keane’s replacement in 2006, less a like-for-like replacement and more a style shift. OK, it could be argued that Berge – an experienced screening No 6 – could step into the Casemiro void after a promising GWC campaign, but Camavinga and Koné like to charge around putting out fires, so perhaps United are following the mould of other top clubs and dispensing with the idea of the Makélélé role.

Modern football is all about excess, whether that be GWC participants, number of games, or transfer fees going beyond £100m for apparently workmanlike players. United have long threatened to descend into financial overspill, but after a steady season under a steady manager, are they finally grasping the concept of modest frugality? Roll up, roll up: ditch the merch-baiting marquee signing and grab yourself three all-purpose midfielders, all for reasonable prices! It surely cannot last.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“This is ideally the high point of my career, of my life, my professional life. I will give it everything I have [but] if you [reporters] tomorrow start saying: ‘He’s sh!t,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away” – Jürgen Klopp takes the Germany job and proves that he should still be good for a quote or two.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp: still got it. Photograph: Markus Ulmer/GES Sportfoto/Getty Images

double quotation mark Re: Simon Mazier’s letter about the location of Iraola’s Amazon parcel (Thursday’s Football Daily). If the delivery guy is anything like ours, the player will turn up at the Etihad” – Dave Eddy.

double quotation mark It would be even worse for Iraola to receive a card saying that his new signing has been left with a neighbour … Everton” – Paul Taverner.

double quotation mark At least if Bezos buys into Liverpool, they get next-day delivery, music, and a TV channel. They can also send back any players they don’t want and get a full refund” – Jeff Bez Peter Arnold.

double quotation mark Matt Targett is staying in the north east with Hull City (yesterday’s email edition)? The north east begins at the River Tees, some 110 miles north of Hull. Geography lessons needed” – Geoff Brodie (and 1,056 others).

Sports.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
Sports.content:
Spain’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has hit out at the “intolerable, unacceptable” behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final.

At the forefront were Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes, who attacked Rodri and Eric García respectively at New York New Jersey Stadium as Spain’s players celebrated winning the World Cup for a second time in the country’s history. Paredes also confronted Spain’s Gavi.

“At the time, I didn’t realise it. I was celebrating, hugging teammates,” De La Fuente told Spanish television. “But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed. Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.”

De la Fuente also praised the exemplary behaviour of his own players faced with these “acts of aggression” and “provocations” which he believes could have escalated into more serious incidents.

Although the scenes were filmed and widely shared on social media, they have not yet resulted in any sanctions against the Argentina players. Fifa has opened an investigation into the incidents to determine whether there may have been violations of the world football governing body’s disciplinary code.

Sports.title: Chelsea paid Aston Villa £117m for Morgan Rogers. Is he the right fit?
Sports.content:
It quickly became apparent this summer that Aston Villa would not be holding on to Morgan Rogers. Having helped the club finish fourth in the Premier League and win the Europa League, the 23-year-old was in demand.

Arsenal looked like his likeliest next destination, with the champions eager to strengthen the left side of their attack. The charm offensive came from many angles, with Martin Ødegaard, Mikel Arteta and the club’s England players trying to sell the idea to Rogers. But, with Arsenal reluctant to meet Villa’s asking price, Chelsea intervened and made Rogers the most expensive British player ever, surpassing the £116m that Manchester City paid Nottingham Forest for Elliot Anderson earlier this summer.

Xabi Alonso is new to Chelsea, so it is difficult to know exactly where Rogers will play. The versatile forward, who started out at West Brom before moving to Manchester City, Middlesbrough and then Villa, will probably be used in a variety of roles – often starting from the left but having opportunities to take up various attacking positions.

Alonso predominantly used a 3-4-3 formation at Bayer Leverkusen and a 4-2-3-1 at Real Madrid. If Chelsea play with three at the back, Rogers will be the left-sided No 10 in the team; if they use a four-man defence, he will start slightly wider but with the freedom to come inside – or he might even occupy the central role.

If Alonso goes with the style he used at Leverkusen, Rogers might not be the best fit. During Alonso’s two full seasons in the Bundesliga, the team averaged 62.1% (2023-24) and 59.6% (2024-25) possession. During their title-winning campaign in 2023-24, they went unbeaten all season while dominating the ball and moving up the pitch slowly.

They were set up to patiently build with lots of passes, win back possession quickly if they lost it and keep the ball as close to the opposition’s goal as possible. They made 367 high turnovers, which was 54 more than any other side. This system works best with attacking players who are tidy and intricate in tight spaces. However, Rogers is at his most effective when he can use his pace and gallop into space.

His dribble completion rate last season was 34.2%, which was nothing to shout about. And his completion rate for passes under pressure was 73.4% – again not exceptional. Of the 161 forwards and midfielders who attempted at least 300 passes under pressure last season, Rogers ranked 143rd. The statistics suggest he is not particularly effective in close-quarters engagements.

With space to attack, Rogers is a threat. He made 223 progressive carries last season, the 10th highest among Premier League forwards, wingers and attacking midfielders. Only Cody Gakpo (41) and Matheus Cunha (35) had more carries that ended in shots than Rogers (30). He also created 16 chances for teammates after a carry: only 11 players created more. Rogers’ combined 46 chances created and shots taken following carries put him behind just Jérémy Doku (58), Gakpo (57) and Bukayo Saka (56). Alonso’s passing style may not bring the best from Rogers.

There are reasons for optimism though. Rogers is frequently on the move and that makes him difficult to track. Only four players made more off-ball runs in the league last season; his 160 off-ball runs ending in the box was the eighth highest in the division.

View image in fullscreen A mural of Jude Bellingham and Rogers in Birmingham. Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The Guardian

He also has the potential to form a good relationship with João Pedro. The Brazilian will probably be the focal point of the team and he is not a conventional No 9. He likes to drop deep, link with teammates and be a creator almost as much as a finisher. With Pedro dropping back, there will be room for Rogers to exploit beyond him: he made 258 runs in behind last season, the 12th highest in the league.

Rogers’ strong relationship with Ollie Watkins bodes well for Chelsea. He created 20 open-play chances for Watkins last season, which was the second most from one player to another in the league. Wherever he has played, Rogers has developed an understanding with his teammates. He already has a close friendship with Cole Palmer after their time together in the Manchester City academy.

Rogers’ other great attribute is his ball-striking ability. Since he made his Premier League debut in February 2024, Rogers has scored 21 non-penalty goals from 14.7 non-penalty expected goals. His overperformance of +6.3 is the 10th highest in the league.

Rogers has a great strike on him and it could be a gamechanger for Chelsea, particularly when they play teams employing a low block. His five league goals from outside the box since his Villa debut is bettered by only six players. Few players are as accurate when shooting from distance. It was his shot against Norway that led to Jude Bellingham’s winning goal in the World Cup quarter-final.

Chelsea have paid an incredible amount of money for Rogers and there are reasons to wonder if the move will work tactically. But Rogers has a habit of making an impact regardless of the context. He’s not a right winger but he still made his presence known for England against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final, setting up Anthony Gordon’s opener from the right.

Is he a £117m player? Perhaps not. Will he succeed playing the same way he played at Villa? Perhaps not. But it’s hard to imagine him not making a significant impact at Stamford Bridge.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Chelsea land Aston Villa coach in shock move – and it’s great news for Morgan Rogers
Sports.content:
Chelsea land Aston Villa coach in shock move – and it’s great news for Morgan Rogers

Aston Villa set-piece coach Austin MacPhee is on the brink of joining Premier League rivals Chelsea, talkSPORT understands.

The 46-year-old joined the club in August 2021 after spells with the Northern Ireland national team, Hearts and FC Midtjylland.



3 MacPhee is heading to Chelsea after five years at Villa Credit: Getty

MacPhee has worked alongside Dean Smith, Steven Gerrard and Unai Emery during his five-year stay at Villa.

However, alongside his assistant manager role with Portugal, he will take his set-piece expertise to Chelsea and work with Xabi Alonso.

He is a highly-regarded coach who is regularly seen on the touchline during matches.



Villa scored 29 goals from set pieces during the 2025/26 season, the joint-most in Europe with Arsenal.

And, as per The Athletic, they have netted 74 set piece goals during his time at the club.



News of MacPhee joining Chelsea comes after Bernardo Cueva was given a new role at Stamford Bridge.

He moved from Brentford before the 2024/25 season to become a set piece coach, but he is now working as a technical analyst.



Worked a treat

MacPhee will be the second arrival at Chelsea from Villa this summer after the British record £117million signing of Morgan Rogers.

The 23-year-old looked set to join Premier League champions Arsenal, but it's Chelsea who completed a deal.

Rogers will therefore work with MacPhee once again in the upcoming season, with the duo already having a successful partnership.

3 MacPhee and Rogers are already accustomed to each other Credit: Getty



During Villa's 4-2 win over Liverpool towards the end of the previous campaign, Rogers opened the scoring shortly before half-time.

His goal, a curling strike into the far corner, followed a well-worked sequence of play from a corner.

The television cameras caught MacPhee celebrating the move, which appeared to have been worked on during training.

Emery joined in with him, with Rogers also seen embracing the coach near the dugout.



Chelsea and Villa business

Whilst Rogers has joined Chelsea and MacPhee is en route, Alejandro Garnacho has gone the other way.

The winger has completed a season-long loan move to Villa, and the deal has a conditional obligation to buy clause included.

3 Chelsea have completed the statement signing of Rogers in a record move Credit: Getty

Nicolas Jackson, who was on loan at Bayern Munich from Chelsea last season, is another player to have been linked with Villa.



They are understood to have been offered the chance to sign the Senegalese striker, who worked with Emery at Villarreal.

Sports.title: ‘Shocking’ – Jude Bellingham’s dig at referee in behind-the-scenes video of Argentina clash
Sports.content:
‘Shocking’ – Jude Bellingham’s dig at referee in behind-the-scenes video of Argentina clash

Jude Bellingham made his displeasure with referee Ismail Elfath clear after England were beaten by Argentina at the World Cup.

The Three Lions went ahead in their semi-final clash but ultimately lost 2-1 as the holders reached the final against Spain, who won.

2 Footage of Bellingham's post-match remark to the referee has been released Credit: Getty

Argentina committed 15 fouls during the match and received three yellow cards, whilst England had one booking from 11 fouls.

It was a feisty affair overseen by MLS referee Elfath, who was making his second appearance at a World Cup.

However, Bellingham took issue with his performance in the middle of the pitch and made it clear after the full-time whistle.

In a video posted by TristanTegtmeyer on TikTok, the ref-cam footage from the match shows Elfath's perspective.

Bellingham walks over to shake hands with the officials and, when he looks to the referee, says: "Some shocking ones, but all the best."

The decisions Bellingham refers to are unknown, but it's evident that Elfath was sub-par in his eyes.

Spilling over at full-time

There was little to no cordiality between England and Argentina at full-time in Atlanta.

Morgan Rogers clashed with opposition players, whilst Bellingham slapped Valentin Barco on the back of his head.

Argentina players then unveiled a banner that read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which means 'The Falkland Islands are Argentina'.

The Falkland Islands are a British Overseas Territory, but Argentina have disputed its sovereignty.

2 Bellingham claimed some of the referee's decisions were shocking Credit: @tristantegtmeyer TikTok

Rules set by the International Football Association Board (IFAB) make it clear that equipment must not have political statements or images.

Peter Kyle, the former Secretary of State for Business and Trade, was on hand to call for an investigation from FIFA.

However, there has been no word from the governing body as of yet, and the White House even defended the players' right to the banner.

Argentina were outplayed in their 1-0 defeat in the final against Spain and sparked a post-match brawl, which saw Leandro Paredes throw punches.

The 2022 champions, who also stood with their backs to Spain when they lifted the trophy, were thoroughly criticised for their behaviour.

Argentina president Javier Milei has since claimed people are 'jealous' of his country despite the players' lack of graciousness in defeat.

Sports.title: Folarin Balogun decision flagged in report about possible World Cup betting irregularities
Sports.content:
Potential betting irregularities have reportedly been linked to Folarin Balogun's controversial red card during the 2026 World Cup.

The striker was dismissed for the United States in their 2-0 last 32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was therefore ineligible to feature against Belgium in the next round.



2 A report has flagged Balogun's red card for potential betting irregularities Credit: Getty

However, as talkSPORT revealed, Donald Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino to review the one-match ban for Balogun, which was later suspended for a year.

Balogun then played against Belgium in the last 16, but the co-hosts were well beaten 4-1.

The decision to suspend his ban was solely taken by FIFA's Disciplinary Committee chairman Mohammad Al-Kamali, which was unusual given that precedent-setting cases tend to have a three-person panel.



Following the conclusion of the World Cup on Sunday, the Council of Europe have released findings from the Group of Copenhagen - who fight against sports manipulation - into possible malpractice.

Across the 104 matches, 15 were 'placed under increased surveillance', with the final day of the group stage being a particular concern.



Another seven were given 'yellow notices' and '12 major controversies' were 'analysed in light of integrity risks'.

The Athletic have reported that the American cryptocurrency-based site Polymarket opened a market that asked 'Will Folarin Balogun play against Belgium?'



This opened on July 2, which is the same day as the United States v Bosnia and Herzegovina match in which Balogun was sent off.

Balogun was confirmed to have been able to play against Belgium by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee on July 5, a day before the match.

It is said that the report from the Group of Copenhagen shows there were no similar markets for any of the 14 other players who were sent off at the World Cup.

2 Balogun was the only red-carded player to have his ban suspended Credit: Getty



Balogun was the only player to have a ban suspended, whilst England defender Jarell Quansah had a one-match sanction for his dismissal against Mexico increased to two matches.

FIFA have been sent an official request by the Group of Copenhagen for a written explanation in regard to the Balogun case.

Another three incidents have been highlighted as potential examples of irregularities, as per The Athletic's report.

This includes the red card for South Africa midfielder Themba Zwane, which he received in the 84th minute of their opening 2-0 defeat to co-hosts Mexico.



Polymarket receiving around $4.8million (£3.6m) from markets on Spain failing to beat Cape Verde in their Group H match, which ended 0-0, also raised concern.

Another flagged example came during Spain's 4-0 group win against Saudi Arabia, during which the VAR team disallowed a goal scored by Ferran Torres after a three-and-a-half minute delay.

Sports.title: Man United told to sell Bruno Fernandes as ‘assists are meaningless’
Sports.content:
Dean Saunders believes Manchester United should sell Bruno Fernandes to fund a summer rebuild, as he dismissed the midfielder's incredible assist record.

Fernandes has been widely hailed as the Red Devils' best player in recent years, and enjoyed an historic 2025/26 campaign by breaking the Premier League record for the most assists in a single season.



5 Bruno Fernandes has been hailed as Manchester United's best player in recent years Credit: Getty

The United skipper set up a huge 21 goals last term, surpassing the previous best shared by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

His stunning individual campaign saw him crowned the Football Writers' Association's (FWA) men's Footballer of the Year, and helped propel his team to an impressive third-place Premier League finish.

But with United now set for a first Champions League campaign since 2024, they have set about bolstering their squad ahead of it.



The Red Devils are in the process of a midfield rebuild, having already snapped up Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos from their Premier League rivals, while they are interested in France duo Aurelien Tchouameni and Manu Kone.

'Brainless'

As Man United weigh up how they will fund any further summer spending, talkSPORT's Saunders pointed to Fernandes.



There is currently no suggestion that the 31-year-old will be going anywhere, as he has a year left on his existing contract, with a one-year extension option.

And while many would label Fernandes indispensable - who has 107 goals and 108 assists in his United career - Saunders was less convinced by his exploits in the latter field.



On Friday's Breakfast Show, he floated around the idea of offloading United's talismanic captain this summer to talkSPORT's Chief Football Correspondent, and Red Devils superfan Alex Crook.

To this, Crook responded: “If you're going to say Bruno Fernandes, the answer is no chance.”

He continued: “21 assists last season. Wears the captain's armband, been the best player by a country mile since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club.

5 Fernandes received the Premier League's Playmaker of the Year award in the 2025/26 season Credit: Getty



“Absolutely brainless to even contemplate that.”

Appearances can be deceptive

Despite Crook's adamant response, Saunders argued that Fernandes' incredible assist statistics could be deceptive.

The former Wales international claimed the Portuguese playmaker's numbers are largely dependent on those around him, insisting his teammates can put him in positions to claim easy assists.

Saunders said: “This assist business, I don't get it.

“I asked Jamie O'Hara the other night, how many assists did you get in your career? He went: ‘I don't know'. I said: ‘Yeah, because no one ever told you and we never counted them’.

“The assists depend on who you're playing with.

5 Fernandes has consistently been United's biggest creator, recording double digits in assists in each of his full seasons at the club Credit: Getty



5 But Saunders wasn't buying his label as the Premier League's top creator Credit: Talksport

"So, for example, if Harry Maguire robs the ball off the centre forward and pokes it to Fernandes and he first times it round the corner for me to go clean through and score, who gets the assist? Harry Maguire or Fernandes? Or both?"

Arguing his case, Saunders insisted Fernandes' upturn in goal contributions was due to him having more clinical players ahead of him.

In the 2024/25 campaign, United recorded a record-low 16th-place Premier League finish, with striker Rasmus Hojlund scoring just four league goals.



By contrast, Michael Carrick's side finished third last term with three of their attacking players hitting double digits in league goals - Bryan Mbeumo (11), Benjamin Sesko (11) and Matheus Cunha (10).

Saunders continued: "If you're playing with Robbie Fowler and you're a left winger, John Barnes, say, and he's whipping crosses in the face of the goal, Robbie Fowler's finishing every cross that comes across - 10 goals, 10 crosses.

“Then he plays with Darwin Nunez, who manages to miss from everywhere. So John Barnes' stats are down because they're not getting finished.

5 Fernandes benefitted from having a more clinical front line in front of him last season Credit: Getty



“Tugay [Kerimoglu] played for Blackburn. He hit Damien Duff's chest on the left wing every five minutes [to then cross] - Damien Duff's [assist] stats were up, and then we signed Andy Cole and his stats went up again because he was finishing them. It's a team game.”

Crook was unable to argue with this, who admitted: “It's made a difference that Fernandes was hitting Cunha and Mbeumo and Sesko last season, and not Rasmus Hojlund.”

No debate

However, Crook was insistent that Fernandes' record-breaking statistics are still incredibly impressive, who also set a new record for the most big chances created in a Premier League season last term.

He added: “To set up 21 goals over the course of a Premier League season is not to be shied away from.”



And the talkSPORT reporter insisted Fernandes' influence at Old Trafford cannot be understated, as he has reached double figures in goal contributions in all of his full seasons at the club.

Crook told Saunders: “Take that away, there's no conversation that since Fergie left the club, Bruno Fernandes has been the most important person at Manchester United."

Sports.title: Leeds immediately sanction exit with James Trafford set to sign
Sports.content:
Leeds United’s pursuit of James Trafford appears to be inching closer with goalkeeper Lucas Perri set for a move to Italy.

The Whites are closing in on the Manchester City shot-stopper Trafford, as reported by talkSPORT on Thursday.



3 Lucas Perri is on his way out of Elland Road after just one season Credit: Getty

Trafford, who secured a move back to the Etihad last summer, has found first-team football hard to come by since the arrival of Gianluigi Donnarumma.

And now an impending move to Leeds is set to be finalised after the club entered into negotiations with Torino for Perri.

The Serie A club have made Perri their first-choice target this summer and are confident of completing a deal for the Brazilian.



According to Fabrizio Romano, just a few details remain before the transfer can be completed.

Perri, who enjoyed a 12-month spell at Lyon prior to moving to Elland Road, is understood to be keen on a move to Italy.



Torino had originally proposed a loan deal for the 28-year-old with an option to buy; however, Leeds are understood to want around £8.5million for the star.

His exit should accelerate Trafford’s arrival at the club with the England international keen on a move to Elland Road.



Trafford had been linked with a switch to Newcastle and almost made the move to St James’ Park 12 months ago.

The Magpies’ interest resurfaced again this summer, but no offer has been tabled for the 23-year-old.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke has long admired the ex-Burnley goalkeeper, who is set to become the club’s first-choice between the posts next season.

3 James Trafford is edging closer to a permanent move to Leeds Credit: Getty



3 Leeds boss Daniel Farke is a long-term admirer of Trafford Credit: AFP

A busy window

Farke has been active so far in the summer transfer window, having added two fresh faces to his squad.

Leeds have wrapped up the signing of Bosnian centre-back Tarik Muharemovic, and he joins free-agent signing Harry Wilson after his departure from Fulham.

Farke led Leeds to a 15th-place finish last season, steering his side away from a relegation dogfight.



The Whites finished nine points above the bottom three thanks to a good run of late-season form.

Leeds kick off their 2026/27 Premier League campaign at Nottingham Forest on Saturday, August 22.

Fixtures against Brentford, Brighton and Newcastle follow for Farke's side, who will be confident of getting early-season points on the board.

Sports.title: New Belgium boss Mark van Bommel recruits ex-Premier League star as assistant
Sports.content:
Mark van Bommel has been appointed as Belgium's new manager on a two-year deal.

The former Netherlands midfielder replaces Rudi Garcia in the dugout, with his contract running until the end of Euro 2028.

3 Van Bommel has been appointed Belgium manager on a two-year deal Credit: Getty

Garcia departed as manager following a quarter-final defeat to Spain at the World Cup.

The Belgian FA subsequently confirmed that his contract would not be extended beyond the tournament.

Van Bommel has now been confirmed as his replacement and will lead the national team in the Nations League as well as Euro 2028 qualifying.

His first match in charge against Italy is scheduled for September 25 before fixtures against both France and Turkey during the league phase.

The 49-year-old had been available after leaving Belgian side Royal Antwerp in 2024.

His two years in charge saw Van Bommel win a league and cup double as well as the Belgian Super Cup.

It followed previous spells with both PSV and Wolfsburg, whilst he has also served as both Saudi Arabia and Australia assistant manager in the past.

As a player, Van Bommel won 79 caps for the Netherlands and was part of the side which reached the 2010 World Cup final.

Coaching staff revealed

Having confirmed his appointment, Van Bommel's Belgium backroom staff has also been revealed.

Amongst them is former Premier League star Boudewijn Zenden.

3 Former Premier League winger Zenden has been named as part of Van Bommel's backroom staff Credit: Alamy

The ex-Netherlands international is a familiar face to fans of Chelsea, Liverpool and Sunderland.

Zenden also played for PSV, Barcelona and Sunderland during his career.

Since retiring in 2011, the 49-year-old has held several coaching roles, most recently with Dutch second-tier side MVV Maastricht.

Meanwhile, he previously served as a coach under Van Bommel at PSV as well as being a team-mate of his at youth and senior international level.

The new manager's coaching team also includes former Belgium midfielder Maarten Martens and Dutch coach Reinier Robbemond.

Van Bommel statement

Following his appointment, Van Bommel explained: "It is a great honour to become head coach of Belgium. I would like to thank the Royal Belgian Football Association for their confidence in me.

3 Van Bommel has been tasked with overseeing Belgium's Nations League and Euro 2028 qualifying campaigns Credit: AFP

"Belgium has outstanding players and enormous potential. Together with my coaching staff, we want to build a team that is disciplined, ambitious and brave enough to compete with the very best.

"Success is never guaranteed, but hard work, honesty and commitment are.

"We will give everything to help this team improve every day and make the Belgian people proud.

"I am looking forward to meeting the players, the staff and the supporters, and beginning this new chapter together."

Van Bommel's first task as manager will be to qualify for the Nations League finals for the first time since 2021.

His side will then be aiming to reach a fourth successive European Championship in two years' time.

Sports.title: Defiant Argentina president claims ‘people are jealous’ as he claps back at criticism of World Cup campaign
Sports.content:
FIFA is investigating Argentina over antics in the World Cup final, but President Milei believes the backlash over his nation's campaign comes down to jealously

Defiant Argentina president claims ‘people are jealous’ as he claps back at criticism of World Cup campaign

Argentina's president has declared people are 'jealous' of his nation amid criticism over the team's World Cup antics.

Javier Milei has been outspoken following La Albiceleste's 1-0 defeat to Spain in the final, and was embarrassed on Monday after he appeared to accidentally publish a scheduled X post celebrating victory.

4 Argentina's president believes many are 'jealous' of the World Cup runners up Credit: Getty

He also bizarrely announced a national holiday that the public might not get, much to the delight of many fans who believed Argentina didn't deserve to win the 2026 tournament based on their negative performances throughout.

A turbulent summer, which featured a row over the Falkland Islands following a semi-final win over England, was capped when Leandro Paredes sparked a brawl by appearing to throw a punch at the final whistle in the World Cup final.

Other players have been described as 'classless' for turning their backs on Spain's celebrations.

Milei, though, believes much of the backlash comes down to jealousy.

"The problem with Argentina is that we are flashy, we don't go unnoticed, people are jealous of us, and we are good at almost everything," the libertarian leader said.

"I'm sorry, but someone had to say it."

Milei watched the final from his home, instead of MetLife Stadium, out of superstition. Argentina still lost the match.

Speaking specifically of the defeat against Spain in an interview with La Nacion, he added: "The match was extremely difficult for us on Sunday, and yet Argentina could have grabbed an equaliser in the final minutes.

"Even though the run of play was not at all favourable, Argentina always took up stances and behaved in a measured manner throughout the tournament.

"Even in the moments when the referee took incorrect positions towards the Argentina national team in some matches, they responded in a very measured and organised way, and they were always distinguished fighting until the end."

4 Milei has praised Argentina for 'distinguished fighting' in the World Cup final Credit: AFP

4 FIFA is investigating the team over their conduct at full-time Credit: Getty

Contrary to Milei's suggestion of a 'distinguished' effort, FIFA has confirmed Argentina are under investigation for their conduct in the World Cup final, and a fan petition calling for the team to be banned for life was recently signed by 23 million people.

Spain head coach says Argentina behaviour 'intolerable and unacceptable'

Meanwhile, Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente has broken his silence on Argentina's conduct after the final whistle on Sunday, and described it as 'intolerable and unacceptable.'

"At the time, I didn't realise it. I was celebrating, hugging team-mates," he told Spanish television.

"But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed.

"Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.

"I want to highlight our behaviour in the face of that kind of aggression and provocation. Our players always kept their composure and behaved like true professionals."

4 De La Fuente has branded Argentina's conduct 'intolerable and unacceptable' Credit: Getty

FIFA has said post-match incidents, which included a Paredes being shown a red card for violent conduct, and Nahuel Molina attempting to knock over Spain midfielder Rodri as he celebrated, are being investigated.

"The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has appointed a Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents," a statement read.

"Further details will be communicated by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee once the prosecutor's report has been completed."

Stay up to date on all things World Cup across our talkSPORT platforms - subscribe to our YouTube channel for the latest news, opinion, exclusive interviews and our daily unfiltered, unscripted show 'The S* Word, from 8am ET.

Sports.title: Spain manager lashes out at ‘intolerable and unacceptable’ Argentina in furious statement after World Cup
Sports.content:
Spain manager lashes out at ‘intolerable and unacceptable’ Argentina in furious statement after World Cup

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente has slammed the behaviour of Argentina players in the moments after his side’s World Cup triumph.

Various tussles took place on the pitch at MetLife Stadium after the final whistle, marring Spain’s 1-0 victory over Lionel Scaloni’s side.

5 Leandro Paredes aggressively hit out at Gavi after the final whistle Credit: Getty

5 But Spain had the last laugh by claiming their second World Cup success Credit: AFP

Argentina stars Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes were seen to be in the thick of the melee as they targeted Spain duo Rodri and Eric Garcia.

The South Americans did not take kindly to the defeat nor Spain’s celebration in the aftermath with Paredes also seen squabbling with Spanish midfield ace Gavi.

What did De La Fuente say about the incidents?

Speaking for the first time about the post-match incidents, De La Fuente hit out at the conduct of Argentina’s stars.

“At the time, I didn’t realise it. I was celebrating, hugging teammates,” De La Fuente told Spanish television.

“But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed.

"Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.”

The Spain boss paid tribute to the behaviour of his players who kept their cool in the face of intense ‘aggression’ and ‘provocation’.

De La Fuente believes the skirmishes could have escalated into more serious incidents.

Argentina are yet to face any disciplinary action despite various angles of the scenes being shared across social media platforms.

FIFA has opened an investigation into the incidents to assess whether Argentina had breached their disciplinary code.

5 Argentina players allowed their frustrations to boil over at full-time Credit: Getty

5 Luis De la Fuente hit out at the conduct of Argentina's stars Credit: Getty

It comes after a petition was launched to inflict a lifetime World Cup ban on Argentina.

In under a week, the petition has garnered a whopping 23 million signatures from 170 countries across the globe.

Fans had become fed up with the South Americans’ antics while accusing FIFA and match referees of 'bias' towards Argentina and captain Lionel Messi.

A new era approaching

Argentina are set for a huge shake up in the wake of last weekend’s World Cup final defeat.

Messi has been tipped to announce his retirement from international football at the age of 39.

Goalkeeper Emi Martinez hinted that he could soon follow suit having played a key role in the past two World Cup campaigns.

5 There will be plenty for Messi to ponder in the coming days and weeks Credit: Getty

Veteran defender Nicolas Otamendi went one better by already announcing his international retirement.

Argentina boss Scaloni’s future is also uncertain after telling reporters that he could call it quits when his contract expires at the end of 2026.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty's wife Holly watches on as star reaches 100m breaststroke final after bizarre 10-minute delay to heats - and local hero Duncan Scott surges to gold
Sports.content:
Four police officers in high-vis vests snuck into the back of the Tollcross stand as Duncan Scott stepped onto the blocks. This was 1:56.38s of sporting theatre that nobody in Scotland wanted to miss.

Scott first dived into this east end pool as a ten-year-old boy. He swam here as a sixth-form student at the 2014 Commonwealth Games but those expectations were nothing like what he felt in Lane two on Friday night.

The sell-out crowd waved their Saltires and roared every stroke as Scott won the hosts' first gold medal of the competition. Adam Ramsay-Peaty was on the same ticket but the locals were here to see one man only.

Scott is the posterboy of these Games and his storming victory in the 200m individual medley provided lift-off. It had a similar feel to Antoine Dupont winning France’s first gold medal on the Sevens pitch at the Paris Olympics, hearing the anthem for the first time.

‘I was a wee bit nervous before that,’ admitted the 29-year-old, who held off a late surge from New Zealand's Lewis Clareburt.

Even the coppers were bouncing. Back in 2014, Scott swam here as a 17-year-old dreamer. He returned as one of the country’s most iconic athletes, ready to add an 11th gold (and counting) to his collection of Olympic, World and Commonwealth medals.

Duncan Scott claimed gold for Scotland in the pool at the Commonwealth Games on Friday

Adam Ramsay-Peaty, meanwhile, eased into the final of the 100m breaststroke in the evening

The locals admire Scott for what he stands for. He campaigns against the closure of local leisure centres – of which Tollcross is one. He lobbies politicians for more funding for public swimming pools and stays true to his principles.

At the 2019 World Championships, for example, he refused to shake hands with Chinese swimmer Sun Yang in protest against his doping conviction.

You suspect Scott would have been Scotland’s flagbearer if his race schedule had not clashed with the opening ceremony. These days, he is held in the same regard as Sir Chris Hoy, his countryman who stepped out of Dr Who’s Tardis with the King on Thursday night.

Scott did not hang around to bask in his glory. The adulation does not come naturally like it does for his contemporary, Ramsay-Peaty. The pair have been room-mates and relay team-mates at the Olympics, enjoying similarly meteoric rises.

With a new name on his swimming cap, Ramsay-Peaty is now hoping to follow Scott onto the medal podium on Saturday night, having qualified for the final of the 100m breaststroke.

His famous wife, Holly, was in the crowd as his qualification faced a bizarre snag. Moments before his first race, one of the lane dividers broke off the pool wall, requiring an official to strip down and jump into the pool to reconnect it.

The amusing 10-minute delay did little to change Glasgow 2026’s image as the Poundshop Games, but at least it did not unsettle the Englishman.

‘In any sport, stuff goes wrong,’ said Ramsay-Peaty. 'It doesn’t help losing all the heat when you’re preparing. There’s ten minutes where you’re losing hydration, I guess, but you know what I’ve done a lot better in worse conditions.

Adam was cheered on by wife Holly, who shared a snap of her view to social media

The couple, who have become a celebrity power couple, were married in December last year

‘Even if it’s a first - scoreboards break, clocks break - the guys got it together pretty well. It was only 10 minutes, right? Hopefully it doesn't happen again. It’s a bit of extra time to enjoy the crowd, I guess. Obviously, I’m a sprinter, so every second counts, but you know what? Stuff happens in sport, stuff happens in life, and you’ve got to get on with it.’

Peaty shared this pool with Scott in 2014. Their journeys have taken different routes, but they seem destined for the same place on the podium.

Sports.title: Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee as Maxence Lacroix has medical ahead of £55m move... and Brentford bid for West Ham wing back: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee as Maxence Lacroix has medical ahead of £55m move... and Brentford bid for West Ham wing back: WINDOW WATCH

For all of yesterday's developments - including Arsenal signing Christos Tzolis in a £34million move from Club Brugge - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Palace eye Le Guen

Crystal Palace have added Raphael Le Guen to their list of options for a new centre back. The 19-year-old plays for Brest in France.

Palace have had bids rejected for Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima and have asked about Trabzonspor’s Chibuike Nwaiwu, who is the subject of offers from Fulham.

Bees buzz around Diouf with Hammers keen to sell

Brentford have held initial talks over a move for West Ham wing-back El Hadji Malick Diouf.

The Senegal international joined from Slavia Prague for £19million and endured an indifferent season.

The Hammers are keen to sell the 20-year-old and expect further enquiries.

El Hadji Malick Diouf made 34 appearances in hs debut season at WestHam

Forest in the market for a safe Beto

Nottingham Forest are weighing up a move for Everton striker Beto.

The Guinea-Bissau international is one of a number of options being considered as Forest look to add a forward for Oliver Glasner.

The 28-year-old scored 10 goals last season as he alternated up front with Thierno Barry, who has attracted interest from RB Leipzig.

Everton would not want to sell without having a replacement in first, while David Moyes wants to bolster his attack regardless.

Chelsea go back to Villa for set-piece coach MacPhee

Chelsea are raiding Aston Villa once again to sign up set-piece coach Austin MacPhee.

The 46-year-old who has also been working with Portugal's national squad, has been at Villa for five years.

He was first given responsibility for set pieces by Northern Ireland national team coach Michael O'Neill and the team scored 11 goals from set pieces in 10 games to qualify for Euro 2016.

He said his farewells to Villa staff today and will link up with the likes of Morgan Rogers once again at Stamford Bridge after Rogers' £117m move this week.

Austin MacPhee with Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo at the World Cup

Moyes pays tribute to Gana Gueye as midfielder leaves Everton for big-money Saudi deal

Idrissa Gana Gueye is poised to take up a lucrative offer to play in Saudi Arabia.

The 36-year-old has now abandoned talks over a new contract with Everton, who confirmed his exit tonight, and as a free agent is in the throes of finalising terms to move to the Saudi Pro League, joining Al-Diriyah.

The Senegal international also had interest from ambitious French side Le Havre but key to his decision apart from the financial gain is a desire to bring up his children in a Muslim country.

Gueye was popular figure at Everton but turns 37 in September.

David Moyes was willing to offer a new contract but wants more energy in his midfield. He has signed Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough and wants two more for his engine room.

As Everton confirmed Gueye's exit Moyes said: 'His leadership qualities in and around the dressing room proved crucial, particularly in our final season at Goodison. His commitment to the club over many years was exceptional.

'Everyone connected to Everton thanks Gana – he will always be welcome at the club – and we wish him and his family all the very best for the future.'

Idrissa Gana Gueye joined Everton in 2022 and has made 120 league appearances for them

Morita's a Tiger as Hull get their man

Hull City have confirmed the signing of defensive midfielder Hidemasa Morita on a free transfer.

The 31-year-old joins on a two-year deal which includes an option for a third. Morita left Sporting Lisbon as a free agent earlier this summer and had been talks with Leeds United and Ipswich Town.

Garner's a no-go as Everton dig in their heels

Everton insist James Garner is not for sale despite mooted interest from Premier League rivals.

The midfielder signed a new contract last season and was rewarded for his form with a call-up to Thomas Tuchel's England squad.

Aston Villa, Newcastle United and his former club Manchester United have all been linked in recent months but Everton have no desire to sell with the 25-year-old a key part of David Moyes's plans.

A string of Premier League clubs have been linked with James Garner, 25

Como set to increase bid for Chalobah

Como are expected to hold talks with Chelsea tomorrow over an improved offer for defender Trevoh Chalobah.

The England centre back is keen on making the move and the Italians - managed by former Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas - have indicated they would increase their bid closer to Chelsea's valuation of £35million including add ons.

Como have so far proposed £25m.

For more on this story click HERE

Lacroix closes in on £55m Chelsea move

Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today after the Blues agreed a deal for the Crystal Palace defender worth around £55m on Thursday.

As Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this week, talks accelerated over a meeting in New York at the weekend.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Palace chairman Steve Parish, who were in New York for the World Cup final, met at the Aman Hotel near Central Park on Sunday.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Chelsea had revisited their interest in the 26-year-old early this summer.

The France international cost Palace £18m from Wolfsburg but has been an outstanding performer in the Premier League and Europe.

Crystal Palace and France star Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today

Villa in talks to sign Jackson

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson.

The clubs have already agreed a loan with obligation deal for Alejandro Garnacho to join Villa. That followed the £117m sale of Morgan Rogers.

The structure of the deals are key as Chelsea and Villa are among those that need to comply with Uefa's squad cost ratio regulations and their 2025 settlement agreements.

Rogers' £117m move will provide Villa with a significant accounting profit, potentially over £80m after Middlesbrough's sell-on clause and the remaining book value of his 2024 signing are deducted.

But if Chelsea had sold Garnacho to Villa as part of the same transaction, Uefa would treat it as a swap deal, impinging on profit margin. Even if Garnacho left on deadline day September 1, that is fewer than the guideline of 45 days, making it harder to argue they are not connected.

A loan with an obligation to buy could still be regarded as part of a swap deal because the 'purchase' has been agreed within 45 days of Rogers' transfer but the conditions give Villa control of when that deal is completed and potential room for manoeuvre with Uefa regulators.

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson

Summerville's Saudi switch confirmed

Al-Hilal have confirmed the signing of winger Crysencio Summerville from West Ham in a deal worth up to £60million.

The 24-year-old, who also had an offer from Roma, had a medical in Amsterdam on Tuesday.

Al Hilal will pay an initial fee of £55m, plus £5m in potential add-ons.

Magpies get their man

Aladji Bamba will wear the number eight shirt vacated by Sandro Tonali, after completing his £30million move to Newcastle United.

Bamba arrived from Monaco on Thursday and Newcastle will pay a further £5.5m in add-ons.

The 20-year-old has signed a five-year contract and manager Eddie Howe said: 'He's another exciting, young signing who we're really looking forward to working with.

Sports.title: Why Joshua Zirkzee might have a future at Man United after all, how Shea Lacey stole the show and the kids shine again: THINGS WE LEARNED as Michael Carrick's men thrash Rosenborg
Sports.content:
Manchester United bounced back from an opening pre-season defeat by Wrexham in Helsinki last weekend by thumping Rosenborg 5-0 in the Lerkendal Stadion in Trondheim.

Head coach Michael Carrick again started with a strong line-up against a side who are 13 games into the Norwegian League season, and the majority of his starting XI stayed on the pitch for an hour as United took a two-goal lead through Shea Lacey and an audacious effort from Joshua Zirkzee.

Carrick then sent on his youngsters who seized the opportunity to impress for the second game in a row and scored three more through Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams.

Perhaps the only disappointment for the United fans in Norway was that teenage star JJ Gabriel didn’t get on the pitch after he was included in the first-team squad for the first time.

Still, there is plenty of excitement to be taken from Friday evening's match.

The Daily Mail Sport looks at what we learned from United’s second pre-season game as Carrick and his players head home from Trondheim ahead of the next friendly against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm a week on Saturday.

Joshua Zirkzee showed why he could still have a Manchester United future with a fine goal

It came as Michael Carrick's side thumped Rosenborg 5-0 in their second pre-season friendly

Zirkzee’s timely reminder

Zirkzee has faced his fair share of criticism since moving to Old Trafford two years ago. The Dutchman has struggled to live up to expectations, and it has never been clear just where he fitted in under Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick.

With United keen to bring in support for striker Benjamin Sesko this summer, they would listen to offers for Zirkzee, but the former Bologna player showed what he can do in Trondheim with a standout display in the win over Rosenborg.

Having set up Bryan Mbeumo for an early chance, he got the assist on Lacey’s opening goal just after the half hour mark. But Zirkzee saved the best for himself in the 56th minute after he started a move from halfway with a pass out to Amass on the left.

The young full-back played the ball back to him, and Zirkzee sold one dummy to bamboozle the Norwegians’ defence and another to leave goalkeeper Rasmus Sandberg on his backside before scoring in an empty net.

For all his critics, Zirkzee possesses the touch and trickery that many players don’t. He just needs to produce an end product on a more consistent basis against the better teams. Maybe he could have a future at Old Trafford yet.

Show-stopper Shea

The talk beforehand had been about the prospect of JJ Gabriel’s first-team debut, but Lacey showed once again what an exciting young prospect he is with an excellent performance in Norway.

The 19-year-old from Liverpool made an immediate impact for the senior side when he got a chance off the bench at Aston Villa in December and rattled the bar as United went in search of an equaliser, but saw his development cruelly cut short when he was handed another opportunity by caretaker boss Darren Fletcher in the FA Cup defeat by Brighton in January when he was sent off for two bookable offences.

However, Lacey re-appeared on the final day, against Brighton again, and he showed his determination to kick on this season after being selected in the senior side that stayed largely unchanged for an hour in Trondheim.

Shea Lacey caused Rosenborg all sorts of problems starting in the No10 role on Friday

Operating primarily in the No10 role behind Zirkzee, Lacey caused Rosenborg all sorts of problems by floating into the pockets and supporting Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu on the flanks.

Moments after playing a part in the move that ended with Dorgu firing just wide of the far post, he put United ahead with a coolly-taken goal. It began on the edge of United’s box with Ayden Heaven who fed Zirkzee, and his pass set Lacey en route to goal.

The youngster was being carefully marshalled by Tomas Nemcik, but cut inside the Rosenborg centre-back and beat goalkeeper Leopold Wahlstedt by guiding the ball inside the far post.

Kids shine again

United’s youngsters followed up a promising performance in Helsinki with an even better display in Trondheim as right back Jaydan Kamason emerged as the pick of the bunch with two assists.

After Devaney had scored from close-range at a corner, Kamason made an overlap on the right before finding Amass who stretched out a leg to score at the back post in the 67th minute. He then tricked his way to the byline to thread another cross to the feet of Williams who tapped in six minutes from the end.

Rosenborg may have made nine changes at half-time and more as the second half progressed in preparation for their next game against Fredrikstad on Monday, but Carrick was delighted with the way United’s kids performed.

‘The younger players came on in the second half, and I thought they were fantastic,’ said the United boss. ‘They played as a team really well and deserved what they got.

‘When you see them expressing themselves and pushing themselves to be better, I was delighted to see that from them. They’ve all got potential in different ways, and you want them to fulfil it and they certainly did that. Some of the goals were fantastic goals, and it was just as pleasing to keep the clean sheet.’

Jaydan Kamason (right) was the pick of the young players that shone as he picked up two assists from right back

Stars are fighting fit

The next game against Atletico Madrid will be a step up for United, and Carrick built his players’ fitness by giving most of them an hour in Trondheim after playing 45 minutes against Wrexham.

Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw went off at the interval, and eight more of the starting XI followed after 60 minutes. Goalkeeper Radek Vitek – one of two changes from Helsinki along with Shea Lacey – stayed on for 70 minutes and was hardly tested aside from one effort that clipped the bar before he was replaced by Dermot Mee.

‘It was a good day,’ said Carrick afterwards. ‘A clean sheet and we scored goals. By the looks of it, everyone coming through injury free is what you want at this stage. I think keeping players fit and progressing through pre-season is as important as anything.

‘Some players need more minutes than others as they go. You're managing some players a little bit more than others. It's never going to be perfect with two weeks in.

‘I think we're in a good place. Four weeks to go until the start, gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress. Moving forward, it's a really good direction to go in.’
